How to Take a Schengen Visa Photo at Home 

Taking your Schengen visa photo at home is straightforward with a modern smartphone and good natural light. Follow these steps, then upload your image to PhotoGov for automatic resizing, background correction, and compliance verification.

Set up the right lighting. Position yourself facing a window or other soft light source. The illumination should be even across your face — no shadows under the nose or chin, no bright patches on your forehead. Avoid using an on-camera flash directly in front of your face.

Prepare a plain background. Stand or sit in front of a plain white wall, a white door, or hang a white sheet. The background should have no visible patterns, textures, or shadows. If you cannot find a perfectly white surface, PhotoGov's background correction tool will adjust it automatically after upload.

Use a tripod or ask for assistance. Position the camera at eye level, approximately 1–1.5 meters (3–5 feet) away. If taking the photo yourself with a front camera, hold the phone at arm's length and ensure it is level with your face to avoid distortion.

Frame and position correctly. Your head and shoulders should both be visible. Look directly into the lens, keep your head level and straight, and maintain a calm, neutral expression — eyes open, mouth closed.

Take multiple shots and select the sharpest one. Do not apply any filters, beauty modes, or retouching before uploading. PhotoGov performs all necessary adjustments to meet official specifications.

Upload to PhotoGov and select "Schengen Visa." The tool will crop the image to the required 35 × 45 mm format, scale the head to 70–80% of the frame, correct the background, and validate all technical parameters. Download the compliant digital photo or a printable two-photo PDF sheet — ready for your visa application.

Schengen Visa Photo for Children 

Children, including infants, must submit Schengen visa photos that meet the same biometric specifications as adult photographs: 35 × 45 mm dimensions, plain white or off-white background, neutral expression, and taken within the past six months. No exceptions are made for children over the age of approximately 12 months.

For infants under one year old, certain practical exceptions apply: the baby's eyes may be partially closed, and a slight mouth opening is generally accepted. Infants may be photographed lying on a plain white blanket, photographed from directly above, or seated in a plain white infant carrier. No other person's hands, toys, pacifiers, or support devices should appear in the frame. The background must remain uniformly white and free of patterns.

Tips for a successful children's Schengen visa photo at home:

  • Timing: Choose a moment when the child is awake, calm, and alert — typically after a nap or feeding.

  • Setup: Lay the infant on a plain white surface with soft, indirect light above; for seated older children, use the same guidance as for adults.

  • Expression: Encourage a calm, open-eyed neutral expression; brief vocal interactions help keep the child focused on the camera.

  • Background: A plain white cot sheet or a plain white wall is an ideal option.

  • Frame: Ensure the child's full face is visible, and no parent's hands, clothing, or accessories are in the shot.

Upload the best image to PhotoGov, and the automated tool will crop, resize, and adjust it to full Schengen compliance without any manual editing required.

10 Common Reasons for Schengen Visa Photo Rejection 

Visa application centers and embassy staff reject Schengen photos more often than any other application document. Understanding the typical failure points allows you to avoid costly delays.

  1. Incorrect dimensions: The image does not measure exactly 35 × 45 mm, or has been cropped to a non-standard aspect ratio.

  2. Wrong background color: Background appears cream, beige, yellow-tinted, grey, or colored — only plain white or near-white is acceptable.

  3. Shadows on face or background: Lighting from the wrong angle creates shadows under the nose, chin, or around the ears, or casts a shadow of the subject onto the background.

  4. Non-neutral facial expression: Smiling, frowning, raised eyebrows, squinting, or parted lips violate biometric standards.

  5. Glare on the glasses in the photo/covered eyes: Though the prescription glasses are generally accepted (double-check with your country), the glare or flash reflection on the lenses is one of the most frequent rejection reasons. If you wear glasses, your eyes must be fully visible, with no glare, no frames covering your eyes, no tinted lenses, no sunglasses.

  6. Head too small or too large: The face occupies less than 70% or more than 80% of the image height, falling outside the 32–36 mm chin-to-crown range.

  7. Photo older than six months: The image no longer reflects the current appearance; any significant change since the photo was taken also requires a retake.

  8. Poor print or image quality: Visible pixelation, compression artifacts, blur, or printing on standard paper rather than professional photo stock.

  9. Digital retouching or AI enhancements: Filters, skin-smoothing, teeth whitening, background alteration that distorts the hairline, or AI face enhancements are not permitted.

  10. Head tilted, turned, or incorrectly positioned: The face must be centered and square to the camera. Slight head tilts are a frequent and easily missed rejection cause.

What to Do IF Your Schengen Visa Photo Gets Rejected

If your Schengen visa photo is rejected by the embassy or visa center, first carefully check the reason stated in the feedback slip or email, as staff usually indicate the exact problem (wrong size, incorrect background, shadows, expression, or glasses). Then retake the photo, making sure it strictly meets the official 35 × 45 mm format, head height of 32–36 mm (70–80% of the frame), plain white or very light grey background, neutral expression, and no eyewear or distracting accessories. 

To avoid repeated refusals, use a professional biometric photo service or an online tool such as PhotoGov that applies the EU Visa Code and ICAO 9303 rules automatically and validates your image before you resubmit your application.

Frequently Asked Questions 

What are the Official Schengen Visa Photo Requirements?

A compliant Schengen visa photo must meet the following official specifications, derived from the EU Visa Code (Regulation EC No 810/2009) and ICAO Document 9303:

  • Size: 35 mm wide × 45 mm high

  • Head height: 32–36 mm from chin to crown (70–80% of image height)

  • Background: Plain white or very light grey, no shadows or patterns

  • Expression: Neutral — both eyes fully open, mouth closed, no smile

  • Recency: Taken within the last 6 months

  • Color: Full-color only

  • Glasses: Allowed, only prescription ones, frames don’t cover the eyes, no glare or flash

  • Print quality: Professional photo paper, matte or glossy, no borders

  • Digital quality: JPEG, 413 × 531 to 600 × 771 px at 300 DPI, max 10 MB.

What is the Schengen Visa Photo Size?

The official Schengen visa photo size is 35 mm wide and 45 mm high — the standard ICAO biometric portrait format used across the European Union. 

  • Schengen visa photo size centimeters: 3.5 × 4.5 cm 

  • Schengen visa photo size in inches: 1.38 × 1.77 inches 

  • Schengen visa photo size in pixels at 300 DPI: 413 × 531 pixels minimum.

What Is the Schengen Tourist Visa Photo Size?

The Schengen tourist visa photo size is 35 × 45 mm, with the head measuring 32–36 mm from chin to crown. This is the same size used for every short-stay Schengen visa.

What Is the Schengen Student Visa Photo Size?

The Schengen student visa photo size is 35 × 45 mm, with the head measuring 32–36 mm from chin to crown. The photo specification does not change between visa types — a study application uses the same photo as a tourist or business application.

What Is the Schengen Business Visa Photo Size?

The Schengen business visa photo size is 35 × 45 mm, with the head measuring 32–36 mm from chin to crown. It is identical to the size used for tourism, study, and all other short-stay Schengen visas.

How Recent Does My Schengen Visa Photo Need to Be?

Your Schengen visa photo must be taken within the six months immediately preceding your application date. The image must accurately represent your current appearance. If you have undergone a significant change in appearance — including major weight change, facial surgery, or substantial change in facial hair — a new photo is required regardless of when the original was taken.

Is the Schengen Visa Photo the Same in All 29 Member States?

Yes. The core specification — 35 × 45 mm size, a 32–36 mm head height, a light background, a neutral expression, and a photo no older than six months — comes from the Schengen Visa Code and ICAO Document 9303. Member states may add small procedural notes, so it is worth checking the page of the consulate or visa center you apply through.

Is the Schengen Visa Photo Size Different from a Passport Photo?

For most Schengen member states, the national passport photo and the Schengen visa photo share identical dimensions (35 × 45 mm) and biometric specifications under EU and ICAO standards. In practice, a photo prepared for your German, French, Italian, or Spanish passport will meet the Schengen visa photo requirements, and vice versa. Always confirm with the specific issuing authority, as minor national variations in background shade or print format occasionally apply.

What Background Color is Required for a Schengen Visa Photo?

The required background is plain white, off-white, or very light grey, uniformly lit and free of shadows, textures, gradients, or visible objects. Cream, warm beige, yellow-tinted, or mid-grey backgrounds will cause rejection. The background must be visibly lighter than the subject's face and hair to ensure adequate contrast for biometric processing.

Are Glasses Allowed in Schengen Visa Photos?

Yes, but only prescription ones, with transparent lenses that don’t have glare, flash reflection, and frames that don’t cover your eyes. The eyes must be fully visible and not enlarged by the lenses (if that is your case, it’s better to take off the glasses for the photo). Prescription glasses, tinted lenses, and sunglasses are prohibited in Schengen visa photos. 

Can I Smile in a Schengen Visa Photo?

No. Even a slight smile is non-compliant if it changes the shape of your mouth or cheeks, or shows teeth. Keep a neutral expression, with the mouth closed, the eyes open, and the facial muscles relaxed, so the biometric measurements stay accurate.

Are Earphones or Headphones Allowed in a Schengen Visa Photo?

No. Earphones, earbuds, headphones, and any other visible electronic accessories must be removed before the photo is taken.

Is a Beard or a New Hairstyle a Problem for My Schengen Visa Photo?

No, as long as the photo is less than six months old and your face is fully visible. A problem arises only when facial hair or a hairstyle covers the jawline, cheeks, eyes, or eyebrows. In that case, adjust your hair or trim your beard and retake the photo.

Do I Need to Remove Facial Piercings for a Schengen Visa Photo?

There is no general ban on facial piercings, but the photo is rejected if jewelry hides facial contours, casts visible shadows, or produces strong reflections. Small, matte studs usually cause no issue, while large rings or shiny metal pieces are best removed for the photo.

Where Can I Get a Schengen Visa Photo Near Me?

Schengen visa photos are available at pharmacies, post offices, retail photo counters, self-service booths, and professional studios in most countries. Online photo tools are an alternative that works from any location at any time and lets you redo the photo immediately if it is not right.

Can I Take a Schengen Visa Photo at Home?

Yes. A smartphone or digital camera with a resolution of at least 12 megapixels is sufficient to capture a technically acceptable image, provided the setup meets official requirements: even lighting, plain white background, neutral expression, and correct framing. The most reliable approach is to take a well-lit portrait at home and then use PhotoGov to automatically crop, resize, and validate it before submission.

What is the Digital Schengen Visa Photo Format and Resolution?

For digital submission via an embassy portal, VFS Global platform, or another online system, Schengen visa photos must be submitted in JPEG (.jpg) format. The minimum recommended resolution is 413 × 531 pixels at 300 DPI (equivalent to 35 × 45 mm in print). Higher resolution — up to 600 × 771 pixels at 300 DPI — is preferred for image clarity. File size limits vary by portal but typically fall between 500 KB and 10 MB. The image must be in 24-bit sRGB color space, with no compression artifacts, filters, or digital enhancements.

How Many Photos Do I Need for a Schengen Visa Application?

Most Schengen visa applications submitted at an embassy, consulate, or in-person visa application center require two identical printed photographs (35 × 45 mm). Some VFS Global and BLS International centers additionally request a single digital file for scanning and data processing. Always refer to the application instructions from the specific embassy or processing center, as requirements vary slightly between member states and application channels.

Can Head Coverings Be Worn in Schengen Visa Photos?

Head coverings are permitted only for religious or medical reasons and only if they do not obscure the hairline, forehead, eyebrows, cheeks, or any part of the face. Religious head coverings (such as hijabs, turbans, or kippot) worn as a daily practice are accepted. Medical head coverings (worn due to illness or post-surgical care) are also accepted, but a signed medical certificate from a licensed practitioner may be required. Fashion hats, caps, beanies, and bandanas are not permitted under any circumstances.

What Clothing Should I Wear for a Schengen Visa Photo?

Wear clean, everyday clothing in solid, mid-tone, or darker colors that provide clear contrast against the white background. Avoid white, off-white, or very pale tops that blend into the background. Uniforms, military camouflage, and anything resembling official or institutional dress are prohibited. Make sure the face and neck remain clearly visible and unobstructed.

Can I Use Makeup in My Schengen Visa Photo?

Yes, natural makeup is permitted provided it does not alter your facial features, skin tone, or structure in any way that would affect biometric identification. Avoid highly reflective or glittery products that may cause unwanted glare under studio or flash lighting. Heavy contouring, theatrical makeup, or face paint that changes the apparent structure of the face is not accepted. Retouching, digital skin-smoothing, and post-processing filters are prohibited.

Are There Different Schengen Photo Requirements for Children and Infants?

The technical specifications — 35 × 45 mm, plain white background, 70–80% head proportion — apply to children of all ages, including infants. For babies under approximately 12 months, ICAO guidelines allow slight relaxation of the expression rule: eyes may be partially closed, and slight mouth opening is generally tolerated. The infant must be alone in the frame, with no visible parents' hands, toys, pacifiers, or support structures. Older children follow the same rules as adults.

What Should My Child Wear for a Schengen Visa Photo?

Dress your child in everyday clothes that contrast with the light background, such as mid-tone or darker tops without large logos or bright patterns. Avoid white tops that blend into the background, anything that looks like a uniform, and any hood, hat, or headband that covers the forehead, ears, or hairline.

What Resolution Should My Schengen Visa Photo Have for Online Submission?

For digital Schengen visa photo submission, use JPEG format at 300 DPI, with pixel dimensions of at least 413 × 531 pixels (35 × 45 mm equivalent). For sharper results and compatibility with high-resolution consulate portals, 600 × 771 pixels at 300 DPI is recommended. The maximum file size is typically 10 MB, though individual portals may set lower thresholds (some VFS Global country portals specify a maximum of 1–5 MB). Color depth must be 24-bit sRGB. Do not apply any compression settings that introduce visible artifacts.

How Do I Check If My Schengen Visa Photo Is Compliant Before Submitting?

Use the PhotoGov Schengen visa photo checker. Upload your image, and the automated compliance engine verifies: exact dimensions and aspect ratio, head-to-frame proportion (70–80%), background color uniformity, presence of shadows, facial expression neutrality, eye openness, and technical file quality (resolution, format, color depth). The system returns instant results indicating whether your photo meets all EU Visa Code and ICAO 9303 standards. Photos created with PhotoGov carry a compliance guarantee: if your image is rejected at the visa center due to a verifiable technical issue, customer support will provide a free retake or full refund.

What Are the Most Common Schengen Visa Photo Rejection Reasons and How Can I Avoid Them?

The most frequent reasons for Schengen visa photo rejection include:

  • Photo dimensions outside the 35 × 45 mm standard

  • Background that is not plain white or very light grey

  • Shadows across the face, neck, or background

  • Wearing glasses of any kind

  • Non-neutral expression (smiling, squinting, raised eyebrows)

  • Head positioned outside the 70–80% frame proportion

  • Photo older than six months

  • Visible pixelation, blur, or poor print quality

  • Digital filters, retouching, or AI skin enhancement

  • Head tilted or turned away from the camera

To prevent rejection, create your photo with PhotoGov: the platform validates every criterion automatically and flags any non-compliance before you download the final file.

Can I Use My Schengen Visa Photo for Another Application?

Yes, within reason. Because the Schengen visa photo uses the standard 35 × 45 mm biometric format, the same photo can usually be used for a European passport, an ID card, or another Schengen visa — as long as it is still within the six-month recency window and reflects your current appearance.

Can I Use a Digital Photo for a Schengen Visa?

Yes. When you apply through an online appointment portal, you upload a digital photo with the application. The file must meet the 35 × 45 mm proportions, be saved as a JPEG, and stay within the portal's file-size and resolution limits.

What Are the Schengen Visa Photo Specifications for Digital Uploads?

For an online Schengen visa application, the digital photo is usually a JPEG, at least 300 DPI, between 120 KB and 10 MB in file size, and up to about 1000 × 1200 pixels. The head should occupy 70–80% of the image. File limits differ between portals, so always confirm the exact figures with the consulate or visa center you are applying through.

Can I Use a Black-and-White Photo for a Schengen Visa?

No. Schengen visa photos must be in color to show natural skin tones and clear detail. Black-and-white and monochrome photos are not accepted.

How Do I Print a Schengen Visa Photo?

Print the photo on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper, with your printer set to maximum resolution. You can print at a photo lab, a post office, a pharmacy photo counter, or at home. A resolution below 300 DPI produces a poor-quality print that is likely to be refused.

Can I Use a Selfie for a Schengen Visa Photo?

Yes, if it is taken correctly. The best results come from placing the phone on a tripod or stand at eye level, using the timer or the rear camera, and producing a straight, undistorted, evenly lit portrait against a plain light background.

Can I Edit the Background of My Schengen Visa Photo?

Yes. You may clean and standardize the background to a plain light tone using an online photo tool, as long as the outline of your head and face is not changed, and no visible artifacts appear around your hair. Editing that smooths skin, reshapes features, or otherwise changes your natural appearance is not allowed.

Can Two People Use the Same Schengen Visa Photo?

No. Every applicant, including each child in a family application, needs their own unique, recent photo. A shared photo, or the wrong photo attached to the wrong applicant, invalidates the application.

A correctly taken photo is an essential part of your Singapore passport application. It must fully meet the official ICA Singapore passport photo requirements: a plain white background, 400 × 514 pixels for online submissions (at 600 DPI and up to 8 MB), or 35 × 45 mm for in‑person applications, along with several other key parameters. Even small mistakes can lead to delays or rejection.

But don't worry. This 2026 guide explains all ICA specifications. There is no need to memorise them: by using a convenient passport photo maker like PhotoGov, you can get an ICA-compliant passport photo from the comfort of your home or office. Visa applications are covered separately, in the Singapore visa photo requirements guide with the ICA specifications for that route.

Source: ICA

We recommend that you download and use mobile apps that are specifically designed to take photographs for passport or identity card applications. These apps usually come with features that will help you take photographs in the required dimensions. The photograph will be accepted if it complies with our photo guidelines.
— The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority Singapore

12 Essential Singapore Passport Photo Requirements: Checklist

The Singapore passport picture requirements are set by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority Singapore (ICA). In turn, they are determined by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) Document 9303 standards. Below is a complete list of 12 essential Singapore passport specifications. The ICA applies separate specifications to visas, and our Singapore visa photo size page prepares that format.

1. Number of Photos

One passport-size photo is required for online submission.

2. Recency

Three months. Accurately reflects the applicant's current appearance.

3. Photo Size

400 x 514 pixels — a digital photo size for an online application via e-Services in Singapore or with a form submitted from overseas. for the printed photo

4. Colour

A colour photograph, naturally reflecting the applicant's skin tone. Over- or underexposed pictures are not accepted.

5. Background

A plain white background, free from shadows, textures, or patterns, is required for ID photos in Singapore.

6. Lighting

Natural, uniform, good lighting that doesn't cast shadows or produce glare on the picture is required.

7. Positioning and Framing

Face and shoulders must be centered, square to the camera, and take about 70-80% of the frame. They must look directly into the camera. The full face, neck, and ears must be visible in the shot and unobstructed.

8. Facial Expression

Neutral facial expression with eyes open and mouth closed is acceptable. Smiling, frowning, or other similar expressions are to be avoided in Singapore ID, passport, or visa photos.

9. Attire, Head Covering, and Accessories

Dress formally. Military and camouflage attire aren't allowed. Head coverings are allowed only if worn for religious reasons and don't obscure facial features. Any attire worn for medical reasons must be supported by an official confirmation letter from a medical provider.

10. Glasses

Glasses are allowed on Singapore passport photos — but only if the frame, glare, or flash reflection doesn't cover the eyes, and they remain fully visible. Tinted glasses, even prescription ones, and sunglasses aren't allowed on ID photos.

11. Print Quality

For offline submissions, the picture must be printed on high-quality photo paper with matte or semi-matte finish (glossy prints are not acceptable).

12. Digital Quality

For digital submissions via e-Services, high-resolution JPG, JPEG, HEIC, HEIF, and PNG photos are acceptable, with a maximum file size of 1-8 MB, and 400 x 514 pixel size.

Unacceptable Singapore Passport Photo Examples

Digital vs Printed Singapore Passport Photo Explained


The format you need depends on whether you submit your application online or in person.

For digital submissions via the ICA Electronic System

, upload a single JPEG file sized at 400 × 514 pixels with a maximum file size of 8 MB.


For physical submissions, prepare two matching prints measuring 35 mm × 45 mm on matte or semi-matte photographic paper. Your face — from chin to the top of your head — must measure between 25 mm and 35 mm within the frame.

Regardless of the submission method, the image must follow the same general guidelines: a plain white background without shadows, a neutral facial expression with mouth closed and eyes open, the head and face occupying 70-80% of the photo, and the image captured within the last three months.

Singapore Passport Renewal Photo Requirements

Below is a list of 7 essential Singapore passport renewal photo requirements (equal to new passport photo submissions):

  1. Photo size: 35 x 45 mm / 400 × 514 pixels without borders, or decorations

  2. Face size: The face must occupy 70-80% of the frame (25-35 mm from chin to crown)

  3. Background: Plain white background free from shadows or patterns.

  4. Recency: Taken within the last three months

  5. Quality: The image should be sharp, clear, and digitally unaltered

  6. Digital properties: JPG, JPEG, HEIC, HEIF, PNG format, up to 8 MB

  7. Expression: Neutral expression, eyes open, and mouth closed.

You can renew your Singapore passport online through the official ICA website.

Baby Passport Photo Requirements in Singapore

Singaporean baby passport photos must follow the same technical specifications as adult photos: 35 mm × 45 mm for physical prints, or 400 × 514 pixels for digital submissions in JPEG format not exceeding 8 MB. The photo must be taken within the last three months, in colour, with even lighting, against a white matte or semi-matte background without shadows or textures. The face should occupy roughly 75 percent of the frame, with approximately 3 mm from the top of the photo to the top of the hair.

Exceptions for infants:

  • Newborns under one month may have eyes partially or fully closed

  • Children under one year may keep their mouths slightly open

  • The baby's head can be supported from behind, provided hands remain completely out of the frame

  • The baby may be laid down on a white sheet instead of having them sit upright.

Setting

Uniform lighting from a natural source, plain background.

Position

A newborn may lie on a blanket; older children — sit or stand.

Expression

Neutral facial expression, no crying or laughing.

Frame

No toys, parents’ hands, or other objects in the frame.

Common Reasons for Singapore Passport Photo Rejection

Many applications get delayed or rejected due to small errors in the photo. The Immigration & Checkpoints Authority lists 10 common issues that cause rejections:

  1. Incorrect dimensions: Photos not meeting the 35 mm × 45 mm print size or 400 × 514 pixel digital specifications​

  2. Non-white background: Any colour, pattern, or shade violates ICA's strict plain white background requirement

  3. Laterally inverted images: Selfies or mirror-reversed photos that flip facial features horizontally

  4. Outdated photos: Images captured more than three months before the application

  5. Shadows or uneven lighting: Shadows on the face, neck, or background, or overexposed/washed-out images

  6. Incorrect facial expression: Smiling, frowning, or any non-neutral expression, rather than a closed mouth and a neutral look

  7. Digital alterations: Any editing, filters, beauty modes, or touch-ups that modify appearance

  8. Poor resolution or blur: Pixelated, blurry, or low-quality images not meeting sharpness standards​

  9. Facial obstructions: Glare on glasses, hair covering eyebrows, or large reflective jewellery obscuring features

  10. Headwear: Hats, scarves, or any other headpieces besides the religious/medical head coverings.

If ICA rejects your passport photo, you will receive notification via letter or email explaining the specific reason for rejection. You have three options to resubmit a compliant photo:

  • By mail: Attach the new photo to the re-submission slip enclosed with the notification letter and mail it to ICA

  • Online: Use the Photo Resubmission service link (if provided in the email notification)

  • In person: Submit it at the Passport Unit's Information Counter, Level 2, ICA Building

Once ICA receives your new photo, processing takes approximately one to two weeks, and you will be notified when your passport is ready for collection.

What are the Singapore Passport Photo Background Colour and Lighting Rules I Must Follow to Avoid Rejection?

Singapore passport photos require a plain white background with even, shadow-free lighting that leaves your face clearly visible. These are the two most common rejection triggers, so following ICA's specifications exactly will help your application proceed without delay.

Background requirements:

  • Colour: Pure white only. Off-white, cream, or grey backgrounds are not accepted.

  • Uniformity: The background must be plain with no patterns, textures, or shadows.

  • Coverage: The white backdrop should fill the entire frame behind your head and shoulders.

  • Shadows: No shadows cast by your head or body onto the background wall.

Lighting specifications:

  • Even illumination: Light must fall uniformly across your face without creating hotspots or dark areas.

  • No shadows: Shadows under the chin, nose, or around the eyes will cause rejection.

  • No red-eye: Camera flash should not produce red-eye effect; retouched red-eye removal is not permitted.

Common mistakes to avoid:

  • Using a cream or off-white wall instead of pure white.

  • Taking photos near windows that create uneven side-lighting or shadows.

Glasses. Remove glasses if possible. If you must wear them for medical reasons, ensure the lenses are clear and untinted with no glare or reflection. Frames must not cover any part of the eyes. Sunglasses and tinted lenses are prohibited.

Head Coverings. Hats and head coverings are generally not allowed. Exceptions apply for religious or medical reasons only if supported by a signed statement from a religious leader or doctor. ICA rejects passport photos that fail to meet strict technical and content standards. The most frequent reasons for rejection are easily avoidable with attention to detail.

Common reasons for rejection:

  • Non-white background: Off-white, cream, grey, or patterned backgrounds are not accepted. Only pure white is permitted.

  • Laterally inverted images: Selfies or mirror-reversed photos that flip facial features horizontally will be rejected.

  • Outdated photos: Images taken more than three months before the application.

  • Shadows or uneven lighting: Shadows on the face, neck, or background, or uneven brightness across the face.

  • Digital alterations: Any editing, filters, beauty modes, or touch-ups that modify appearance.

  • Poor resolution or blur: Pixelated, blurry, or low-quality images.​

  • Facial obstructions: Glare on glasses, hair covering eyebrows, or large reflective jewellery obscuring features.

How to ensure your photo meets requirements:

  • Use a plain white wall as the backdrop and position yourself about one metre away to avoid shadows.

  • Ensure even lighting from the front without harsh shadows or red-eye.

  • Take the photo within three months of your application date.

  • Face the camera directly with a neutral expression and mouth closed.

  • Avoid any digital editing or filters; submit the original image.

  • Verify dimensions: 35 mm × 45 mm for prints or 400 × 514 pixels for digital uploads.

  • Remove glasses if possible, and keep hair away from your face.

Are There Different Singapore Passport Photo Requirements for Children and Infants, and What Should Parents Prepare?

No, the technical specifications remain identical for applicants of all ages. Children and infants must submit photos measuring 35 mm × 45 mm for prints or 400 × 514 pixels for digital submissions, with the same white background and lighting requirements as adults.

However, there are a few less strict rules for younger children:

  • Newborns under one month: Eyes do not need to be fully open.

  • Infants: May be photographed lying on a white sheet instead of sitting upright.

  • Support: Parents may support the baby's head, but hands must not be visible in the final photo.

  • Expression: Neutral expression is preferred, but mouths may be slightly open for children under one year.​

  • Prohibited items: No toys, pacifiers, bottles, or other objects may appear in the photograph.

Below is a list of 11 essential Singapore passport photo requirements for digital photo uploads to ICA E Services.

  1. Dimensions: 400 × 514 pixels (width × height)

  2. File format: JPEG (.jpg) only​

  3. File size: 1-8 MB

  4. Resolution: Minimum 600 DPI

  5. Colour mode: Full colour (no black-and-white, sepia, or filters)​

  6. Recency: Taken within the last 3 months

  7. Background: Plain white without patterns, textures, or shadows

  8. Lighting: Even illumination with no shadows on face or background

  9. Face size: the face must occupy 70-80% of the photo height

  10. Position: Full face, front view, centred in the frame

  11. Expression: Neutral with no smile, mouth closed, and eyes open.

Additional rules:

  • No headgear unless worn for religious or medical reasons (must not cover facial features)

  • Glasses permitted only if eyes are clearly visible with no glare or reflection; no tinted lenses

  • No digital editing, filters, or alterations to the original image​

  • Scanned prints are not accepted; must be original digital capture.

Can I Smile In A Singapore Passport Photo?

No. You must keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed and eyes fully open. Broad smiles, visible teeth, or exaggerated expressions are not allowed because they change how your face looks and can lead to rejection.​

Are Glasses Allowed In A Singapore Passport Photo?

Yes, but only if they do not obstruct your eyes. The frames must not cover the pupils, there should be no glare or reflections on the lenses, and the lenses cannot be tinted; sunglasses and dark prescription lenses are never permitted.​

Can I Wear A Headscarf, Turban, Or Other Head Covering?

Yes, when it is worn for religious or medical reasons. The covering must not hide any part of your face from chin to forehead and should not cast heavy shadows or obscure your features.​

No. Beauty filters, strong retouching, or skin‑smoothing tools are not allowed, and the photo must show your natural skin tone and real appearance so immigration officers can recognise you easily.

When you apply for a Singapore visa, pay extra attention to the quality of the photo that you submit with your application. Singapore has strict rules for biometric photos: 35×45 mm or 400×514 pixels, plain white background, taken within the past three months, printed on matte or semi-matte photo paper, and other important parameters. An incorrectly taken image can lead to visa rejections or delays. For the passport itself, you can make a Singapore passport photo online from the same selfie.

But worry not, this 2026 Singapore visa photo requirements complete Guide covers all the specifications you need to meet, from exact dimensions and digital formats to clothing rules and common rejection reasons. Whether you are visiting a professional studio or taking the photo yourself at home, following these guidelines will help your application proceed without unnecessary delays.

Source: ICA

“We recommend that you use mobile apps or platforms designed specifically for passport or identity card photographs. These tools help applicants produce images in the required dimensions. The photograph will be accepted if it complies with our guidelines.”

— Immigration & Checkpoints Authority Singapore

11 Essential Singapore Passport Photo Requirements: Checklist

The Singapore visa photo requirements are defined by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority Singapore (ICA) and follow the biometric standards of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO). We created this Checklist with 12 passport photo requirements to help you smooth the application process and produce an acceptable photo on the first try. The rules for Singapore passport photos come from the same ICA framework and are collected on a separate page.

The good news is that you don’t need to memorise each one of them: our passport photo maker, PhotoGov, is designed to apply them automatically to your selfie. Simply upload it to our platform, and get a technically correct, 100% ICA-compliant, and application-ready Singapore visa photo.

Requirement

Specification

1. Number of Photos

One visa photo is required for online applications. Visa centres may require 1-2 identical prints (check your provider's instructions).

2. Recency

The picture must be taken within the past three months and reflect the applicant's current appearance. A new photo must be submitted for each application; previously used photos are not accepted.

3. Photo Size

35×45 mm (1.38×1.77 inches) for printed photos; 400×514 pixels for online photo submission through e‑Services or overseas missions. The applicant's head must occupy 70-80% of the frame (25-35 mm).

4. Colour

A colour photograph with natural skin tone and accurate exposure is required. The photo must be clear, in focus, and free from any reflections or shadows. Overexposed or underexposed images are rejected.

5. Background

A plain white background without shadows, patterns, or texture.

6. Lighting

Uniform lighting with even brightness, free from glare, shadows, or overexposure.

7. Positioning and Framing

The applicant's face and shoulders must be centered in the frame. Eyes directed at the camera, with the full face, neck, and ears visible.

8. Facial Expression

A neutral facial expression with both eyes open, and the mouth closed, looking directly into the camera. Smiling or frowning is not permitted.

9. Attire and Head Coverings

Appropriate everyday attire in darker colours is required. Head coverings are permitted only for medical, religious, or racial purposes — and only if they don't obscure facial features. Hair should not cover the face or eyes. Uniforms are not allowed in visa photos.

10. Glasses

Allowed — but only if there is no reflection or glare on the lenses and the frames don’t cover the eyes. Tinted lenses (even prescription ones) or sunglasses are not accepted.

11. Print and Digital Quality

For in-person applications, the physical copies must be printed on high-quality photo paper with a non‑reflective (matte or semi‑matte) finish. For ICA e‑Services, accepted formats include JPG, JPEG, HEIC, HEIF, and PNG, with a maximum file size of 8 MB and a 400 × 514 pixel size. The digital photo must be high‑resolution and free of pixelation.

Singapore accepts both formats, depending on your application method. Digital files are uploaded directly through the ICA portal for online submissions. Printed photos are attached to paper applications submitted at authorised visa centres or embassies.

For babies, authorities usually accept more flexibility: infants under one year may have their eyes closed, but the image must still follow the same size, background, and quality standards as any other Singapore visa photo.

How to Apply for a Singapore Visa?

You need a valid visa to be officially granted access to Singapore, and an arrival card — to enter the country physically.

Make sure that all information is accurate and that their application is complete before submitting it to avoid delays or rejection.

Submit your visa application online via e-Service, Singapore Overseas Mission, or through authorized visa agents, paying a non-refundable visa processing fee.

If your visa is approved, apply for a Singapore Arrival Card (SGAC) via e-Service or My ICA Mobile app within three days before you enter Singapore. The SGAC application is free, and you typically receive it in your email within a few hours.

The processing time for a Singapore visa application is 3 to 5 working days. After submission, ICA officers will review your application, supporting documents, and verify that the photos meet the official requirements. Check the application status online, using your reference number.

Important Note: Apply for your visa at least 30 days prior to your visit to Singapore.

Common Reasons for Singapore Visa Photo Rejection

The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) most frequently flags the following 10 issues for visa photo rejections:

  1. Incorrect size and head height: Printed photos not measuring exactly 35 mm × 45 mm, or head size outside the 25-35 mm chin-to-crown limits. Digital files that aren’t exactly sized 400 × 514 pixels

  2. Incorrect background colour: Background that is off-white, cream, coloured, patterned, or textured instead of a plain white backdrop without shadows.

  3. Outdated photos: Images taken longer than 3 months ago or no longer matching your current appearance (for example, after major changes to facial hair or hairstyle).

  4. Shadows or uneven lighting: Visible shadows on the face, neck, or background, or strong highlights that wash out facial features.

  5. Wrong facial expression: Smiling broadly, frowning, tilting the head, or not looking straight at the camera instead of a neutral, front-facing pose with eyes open and mouth closed.

  6. Digital retouching and filters: Beauty modes, skin-smoothing, colour filters, red-eye correction, or any edits that alter natural appearance.

  7. Blur, noise, or low resolution: Grainy, pixelated, out-of-focus, or low-quality images that don't show clear facial detail. Digital files with low resolution (below 300 DPI) or larger than 8 MB.

  8. Obstructions on the face: Hair covering eyes or eyebrows, heavy glare on glasses, tinted lenses, or large jewellery hiding facial contours.

  9. Head coverings and accessories: Fashion hats, caps, or non-religious/non-medical headwear that conceals the hairline or casts shadows. Religious headwear must not obscure facial features.

  10. Poor print quality: Home inkjet prints, streaks, colour casts, creases, fingerprints, or damage to the photo surface. Incorrect paper type (glossy instead of matte or semi-matte) or photos with white borders.

If ICA rejects your Singapore visa photo, you will receive notification explaining the specific reason via your submission channel (embassy, consulate, accredited agent, or the ICA e-Visa portal). A successful Thailand e-Visa application relies on the quality of the photo you upload with it. If you are applying online through thaievisa.go.th, upload a digital JPG or JPEG under 3MB, taken within the last six months. If you are submitting a paper application at a Thai embassy or consulate, you must submit a printed 35×45 mm photo (but please keep in mind that some missions, like the Royal Thai Embassy in Singapore, require a 40x60 mm photo, so always double-check the exact specs at your Thai embassy, consulate, or visa center). 

This guide covers 2026 Thailand visa photo requirements in detail for online and offline applications. 

Source: thaievisa.go.th

11 Essential Thailand Visa Photo Requirements: a Checklist

Thailand e-Visa photo requirements are based on the official instructions provided by thaievisa.go.th, the visa portal of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Thailand. The official user manual confirms the accepted file format, the 3MB file size limit, and the six-month recency rule at the “Upload Photograph” step. For an application-ready result, prepare the photo in the standard 35×45 mm format and follow ICAO Document 9303 guidelines for biometric photo composition. Always double-check the exact requirements of your mission, as some of them ask for a 40 x 60 mm photo with a Thai visa application.

Requirement

Details

1. Recency

The photo must be taken within the last six months. thaievisa.go.th states that failure to meet this may result in rejection of the visa request

2. Thailand Visa Photo Size

3.5 x 4.5 cm — the most common format. However, the Royal Thai Embassy in Singapore's e-Visa photo specifications page requires a 4 x 6 cm (472 x 709-pixel) photo. Since Thai missions don't apply a single uniform size across all locations, confirm the exact dimension requested by the specific embassy, consulate, or entry point you're applying through.

3. Color

The image must be in color and accurately reflect the applicant's natural skin tone and hair color

4. Background

A plain, white, evenly lit background

5. Lighting

Even, natural lighting without harsh shadows

6. Positioning and Framing

Face the camera directly, with head and shoulders square to the camera

7. Facial Expression

A neutral expression with eyes open, mouth closed

8. Attire, Head Covering, and Accessories

Remove headwear and heavy accessories that may obstruct your facial features, hairline, or neck

9. Glasses

Allowed if the frames don’t obstruct your eyes and there is no glare on the lenses. Sunglasses and tinted lenses aren’t allowed. The safest practice is to remove glasses before taking a visa photo

10. Thailand e-Visa Digital Photo Requirements

JPG or JPEG format, file size under 3 MB

11. Print Quality (Paper Applications)

Usually, two photos printed on photographic paper are required, with no marks or creases. If you're applying on paper at a Thai embassy or consulate, check that mission’s requirements.

Infants and Babies Under 1

We recommend following the general ICAO Doc 9303 guidelines for newborns and babies under 1 year old: photograph the baby lying down on a plain, light-coloured surface, camera positioned directly above, face centred and clearly visible. It is generally acceptable for a very young baby's eyes not to be fully open, as long as the facial features are clear and recognisable.

Toddlers and Young Children

For toddlers, the priority is an unobstructed, clearly visible face. A perfectly neutral expression can be difficult to achieve at this age; a natural, relaxed look is acceptable as long as the child faces the camera directly, with no toys, hands, or other people visible in the frame.

Older Children

Older children should follow the same standard as adults: facing the camera, neutral expression, eyes open, mouth closed, head and shoulders within the frame.

Common Reasons for a Thailand Visa Photo Rejection

Below are the reasons most likely to cause a Thailand visa photo rejection, based on the information from the Thai eVisa official website.

  1. Wrong file format. The portal accepts JPG or JPEG only. A PNG, HEIC, or other format will be rejected by the upload system.

  2. File too large. The file must be under 3MB. An oversized file won't upload.

  3. Photo older than six months. thaievisa.go.th states directly that this may result in rejection of the visa request.

  4. Low image quality. Blurred focus, heavy compression, or visible pixelation are common technical rejection causes for any digital upload.

  5. Obstructed face. Sunglasses, hats, or hair covering the face interfere with the biometric composition ICAO Doc 9303 expects, even though Thailand doesn't publish this rule explicitly for the e-Visa.

If your PhotoGov photo is rejected by authorities, contact Customer Support immediately. We will investigate the cause, and if it stems from a technical error on our end, you will receive a full refund and a free retake.

Who Needs a Thailand Visa and How to Apply

Whether you need a visa to enter Thailand depends on your nationality and the purpose and length of your trip — some nationalities can enter visa-free or apply for a visa on arrival, while others need to apply in advance. Thai eVisa official website includes an eligibility check where you enter your nationality and travel details to see what applies to you; check it before assuming you do or don't need a visa.

You can apply for a Thailand visa through:

  • The official e-Visa portal

  • A Thai embassy or consulate, for a paper application

Documents Required for a Thailand Visa Application

Exact document requirements vary by visa type and nationality — check the current list on the Thai eVisa official website for your specific case. In general, an e-Visa application asks for:

  • A valid passport, scanned at the biodata page

  • A recent digital photo meeting the specifications above

  • A completed online application form

  • Supporting documents specific to your visa category and nationality

Frequently Asked Questions

What Size and Dimensions Are Required for Thailand Visa Photos?

Though thaievisa.go.th does not publish a specific millimetre or pixel size for the e-Visa photo, the widely used format for Thai visa photos is 35 x 45 mm. But please beware that some missions, for example, the Royal Thai Embassy in Singapore, require a 40 x 60 mm photo with Thailand visa applications — always double-check the exact specs before applying! When you submit it for your eVisa, the file must be a JPG or JPEG under 3MB, taken within the last six months.

What Are the Current Thailand Visa Photo Requirements for a Successful Application?

Your Thailand e-Visa photo must be a recent, color, plain-background image that clearly shows your face. Here's what the photo needs to meet:

  • Recency: Taken within the last 6 months.

  • Size: Not explicitly published by the e-Visa portal, but 35 x 45 mm (3.5 x 4.5 cm) is the recommended and widely accepted standard, matching Thai consular photo requirements. However, some missions may require 4 x 6 cm photographs for Thailand visa applications — always double-check before submitting.

  • Color: Full color, accurately showing your natural skin tone and hair color.

  • Background: Plain white or off-white, evenly lit with no shadows.

  • Expression: Neutral, mouth closed, both eyes open, facing the camera directly.

  • Head and shoulders: Squared to the camera, full face visible from hairline to chin.

  • Headwear: Not allowed, except for items worn daily for religious reasons.

  • Glasses: Allowed — just make sure the flash doesn't create glare on the lenses.

  • Digital file: JPG or JPEG format; check the exact file-size limit on your upload screen, since the portal's stated cap can vary.

  • Printed photos: If applying on paper at a Thai embassy or consulate, bring two prints on photographic paper, free of marks or creases.

What Are the Background Color and Lighting Requirements for Thailand Visa Photos?

Your Thailand visa photo needs a plain, solid white background with even lighting and no shadows, reflections, or visible texture behind you. Sit or stand at least a foot away from the wall to avoid a shadow falling on the background, and use soft, diffused light rather than a direct flash or overhead spotlight, which can wash out your features or create harsh contrast. PhotoGov applies this exact background and lighting standard automatically when you upload your photo, replacing an uneven or colored backdrop with a compliant plain white one.

Where Can I Get a Thailand Visa Photo Taken That Meets All Requirements Near Me?

A professional photo studio, passport-photo print shop, or photo kiosk at a pharmacy or convenience store can produce a properly lit, plain-background color photo in the correct 3.5 x 4.5 cm (or, depending on a mission, 4 x 6 cm) size. For the e-Visa specifically, you'll also need the shot as a digital JPG or JPEG file under 3 MB — not just a printed copy — so confirm the studio can email or export it as a file, or scan the print and run it through an online photo tool to convert it to the right format and size. If you're applying in person at an embassy or consulate that still accepts paper applications, ask the studio for two printed copies as well, since some missions request both formats.

Can I Smile in a Thailand Visa Photo?

Keep your expression neutral, with your mouth closed and both eyes open, rather than smiling. Thai visa photos follow the standard used for biometric ID and passport photos worldwide: a natural, relaxed face without a wide smile, since an open-mouth expression can distort the facial measurements used to verify your identity against your passport and other travel documents.

Can I Wear Glasses in My Thailand Visa Photo?

It's best to remove your glasses for a Thailand visa photo. While policies differ slightly by mission, several Thai consulates explicitly instruct applicants not to wear eyeglasses or dark glasses in their visa photo, since lenses can create glare or reflections that obscure the eyes. Removing them before your photo is taken avoids this risk entirely and keeps your application consistent with the strictest interpretation applied across Thai missions.

How Do I Take a Thailand Visa Photo at Home?

Stand about an arm's length from a plain white wall in a well-lit room, ideally near a window during daytime for soft, natural light. Have someone else take the photo straight-on at eye level, or use a tripod and timer to avoid the angle distortion of a handheld selfie. Once you have a clear, front-facing shot, upload it to an online Thailand visa photo maker like PhotoGov, which crops it to 3.5 x 4.5 cm (default Thai visa size), corrects the background, and exports it as a JPG under 3 MB, ready for the e-Visa portal upload — just make sure the source photo was taken within the last six months.

Can I Apply for a Thailand Visa on Paper Instead of the e-Visa Portal?

Yes. Photo requirements for paper applications are set individually by each mission rather than by thaievisa.go.th, so specifics like print size, number of copies, or acceptable background can vary slightly from one embassy to the next — always confirm directly with the consulate handling your application before printing your photos.

acceptedAnswer.text: Though thaievisa.go.th does not publish a specific millimetre or pixel size for the e-Visa photo, the widely used format for Thai visa photos is 35 x 45 mm. mainEntity.name: What Are the Current Thailand Visa Photo Requirements for a Successful Application?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Thailand e-Visa photo must be a recent, color, plain-background image that clearly shows your face. Here's what the photo needs to meet: Recency: taken within the last 6 months. Size: not explicitly published by the e-Visa portal, but 35 x 45 mm (3.5 x 4.5 cm) is the recommended and widely accepted standard, matching Thai consular photo requirements; however, some missions may require 4 x 6 cm photographs for Thailand visa applications — always double-check before submitting. UAE Passport Photo Requirements 2026, Updated and Expert-Verified

A UAE passport photo is a biometric image that meets a strict set of technical specifications — 40 x 60 mm or 945 x 1417 pixels, plain white background, taken within the last 6 months, and other essential parameters. This 2026 Guide covers all official UAE passport photo requirements to help you avoid delays, repeat submissions, or reappointments. Residence documents follow their own specifications, and the Emirates ID residence visa photo requirements are covered on a separate page.

Source: ICP

11 Essential UAE Passport Photo Requirements: Checklist

Defined by the Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP), UAE passport photo requirements are based on the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303 standards. Visitors applying for entry should use our guide to UAE visa photo rules instead, where the size is 43 x 55 mm.

In this section, we focus on 11 core requirements you should check before submitting your picture for an Emirati passport. Today, with convenient tools like PhotoGov, you do not need to memorise all of them — you can use our passport photo maker to turn your original portrait into a 100% compliant, application-ready UAE passport photo.

Requirement

Specification

1. Number of photos

One digital photo is required for a UAE passport application.

2. Recency

Taken within the last six months, reflecting the current appearance of the applicant. If they have undergone a significant appearance change, such as weight loss or plastic surgery, the most recent picture is required for the application.

3. UAE passport photo size

40 × 60 mm (1.57 × 2.36 in) or 945 × 1417 pixels. The required head size is 70-80% of the image.

4. Color

The UAE passport photo must be in color, naturally reflecting the applicant's skin tone and hair color.

5. Background

A plain white background is required for a UAE passport application. It must be free from shadows, patterns, and any other distractions.

6. Lighting

Uniform lighting is required for UAE passports — no harsh shadows, reflections, or red‑eye effect can be present in the photo.

7. Positioning and framing

The photo must not have a frame. Face and shoulders must be square to the camera, with only the upper part of the shoulders visible.

8. Facial expression

A neutral facial expression is required — the applicant must keep their eyes open, and mouth closed, and look directly into the camera. Avoid unnatural expressions, as well as smiling or frowning, on ID, passport, and visa photos.

9. Attire, head covering, and accessories

Everyday clothing in colors that contrast with the background is required. Attire customarily worn for religious purposes is permitted, provided it does not obscure facial features. The same applies to head coverings worn for religious or medical reasons. Accessories such as jewelry may be kept if they do not cover any part of the face or hairline.

10. Glasses

Glasses should be removed in the UAE passport photo. Tinted glasses — including prescription ones — and sunglasses are prohibited. Applicants who wear glasses or eye patches for medical reasons, such as following eye surgery, must include a signed statement from their treating hospital or medical provider.

11. Digital quality

Digital photos must have a resolution of 600 DPI, 945 × 1417 pixels, saved as JPG, with a file size of 1-15 MB. A UAE passport picture should be in focus and free from shadows, filters, or any visible printing or compression marks.

What Shall I Wear for the Arab Emirates Passport Photo?

Wear your everyday clothes, preferably in darker, solid colours. Avoid white or very light tops that blend into the background, as well as overly bright patterns or logos that may distract from your face. Uniforms or camouflage-style clothing are prohibited in official photographs.

The hairline and the neckline must be open and visible in the photo. Clothing and head coverings worn for religious reasons are allowed, provided your entire face remains clearly visible. Medical head coverings are also permitted, as long as they do not cast shadows on your face or obscure any facial features. In this case, you must provide a letter signed by your medical provider, explaining the need for a medical headpiece.

As for accessories, the general rules apply: they must not cover facial features or cast shadows. Large earrings, necklaces, or piercings must be removed.

Where to Take a Passport Photo in the UAE

Passport photos in the UAE can be taken at professional photo studios, authorized printing centers, and major retail chains offering ID photo services. Customer Happiness Centers and ICP offices across the Emirates provide on-site photo services for submitting passport or ID applications.

United Arab Emirates Passport Photo Requirements for Children

For UAE passports, baby photo rules are almost the same as for adults, with a few practical differences. The picture must be in colour, recent, on a plain light background, and the baby’s face should be clearly visible and turned towards the camera.

Unlike adults, babies are not expected to keep a perfectly neutral expression, and slightly open eyes are usually accepted for newborns. You can simply photograph your baby at home on a light blanket or against a plain wall. No hands, toys, or other objects can appear in the frame, and nothing should cover the face, so remove hats, headbands, hoods, and pacifiers before taking the photo.

There are four options for the Emirati citizens to obtain passport services:

  1. Online via the ICP eServices portal

  2. Through the UAEICP mobile application, available on Google Play and the App Store

  3. At Customer Happiness Centers located across the country

  4. At the passport service counters in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, and Sharjah airports, which operate around the clock, but only on an emergency basis.

When applying online, you must submit your Arab Emirates passport photo in a digital version. When applying in person, submit photos printed on high-quality photo paper.

Passports for Emirati newborns are issued through the Mabrouk Ma Yak program that simplifies the registration of a child’s birth and the issuance of all essential identity documents.

NOTE: Parents can receive the newborn’s birth certificate, Emirates ID, and passport in one streamlined application without submitting separate applications to different authorities.

Common Reasons for UAE Passport Photo Rejection

The Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship (ICP) most frequently flags the following 10 issues that can lead to a passport photo rejection:

  1. Incorrect size and proportions: Images not within the required 40 mm × 60 mm / 945 × 1417 pixels dimensions

  2. Improper background colour: Background that is not plain white, or has shadows, patterns, textures, or uneven lighting instead of a clean, uniformly white backdrop

  3. Shadows on face or background: Visible shadows on the face, neck, or background that interfere with biometric recognition systems

  4. Wrong facial expression: Smiling broadly, frowning, tilting the head, or not looking straight at the camera

  5. Incorrect file format and resolution: Submitting a digital photo in an incorrect format (PNG instead of JPG), dimensions, and resolution below 600 DPI

  6. Obstructions on the face: Hair covering eyes or eyebrows, heavy glare on glasses, tinted lenses, or accessories that hide facial contours or the hairline

  7. Improper clothing: large logos, clothing resembling military attire, or items that blend with a white background

  8. Digital enhancements: Any digital retouching applied to the image, including colour correction, brightness adjustments, or automatic enhancement features

  9. Laterally inverted image: photos with digitally switched left and right sides of the face.

  10. Outdated photos: taken more than 6 months before the application, or photos that don’t show the applicant’s current appearance if they have undergone a significant appearance change.

What to Do if Your UAE Passport Photo is Rejected

If your UAE passport or Emirates ID photo is rejected, the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Port Security (ICP) will notify you by SMS or through your online account, stating why the image was not accepted and asking you to upload a replacement.

To avoid further delays, fix the specific problems mentioned (such as background, lighting, or size) and resubmit a new compliant photo via the ICP website or mobile app, or, if you applied in person, through an ICP Customer Happiness Centre or authorised typing centre.

Your application will only move forward once a suitable photo has been provided, so it is important to respond to the rejection notice promptly.

requirements/uae-visa-photo-requirements.content:
A successful UAE visa application relies on the quality of the photograph that you submit with it. Sized 43 x 55 mm or 1016 × 1300 pixels, it must have a plain white background, no frames or digital enhancements, and follow a few other essential specifications. Our complete 2026 UAE visa photo requirements Guide covers them all, so you can create a technically compliant, application-ready photo. Residence applicants can prepare an Emirates ID residence visa photo on its own page.

Source: ICP

11 Essential UAE Visa Photo Requirements: a Checklist

Emirates visa photo requirements are determined by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs, and Port Security (ICP). In turn, they follow the biometric standards established by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO). Only official photos that match the 11 specifications listed below are accepted with UAE visa applications.
The ICP sets separate specifications for travel documents, collected in our UAE passport photo rules 2026 guide.

Requirement

Details

1. Recency

The photo must be taken within the last six months and accurately reflect the applicant's current appearance.

2. UAE Visa Photo Size Requirements

43x55 mm (1.69×2.17 inches), with the face size measuring between 31 and 44 mm (1.2-1.7 inches), or approximately 70-80% of the image height.

3. Color

The image must be in color and accurately reflect the applicant's natural skin tone and hair color.

4. Background

Plain white background with no shadows, patterns, or objects visible in the frame.

5. Lighting

Even, uniform lighting. No shadows or reflections can be present in the image, neither on the applicant's face nor in the background.

6. Positioning and Framing

The applicant must face the camera directly, with head and shoulders square to the camera. No borders or margins are allowed.

7. Facial Expression

A neutral facial expression is required for visa and passport applications — eyes open, mouth closed. No smiling, frowning, or any other exaggerated facial expressions are allowed.

8. Attire, Head Covering, and Accessories

Regular clothes that don't blend with the background are required. Military or camouflage wear isn't allowed. Religious attire worn daily is acceptable if it doesn't obstruct the face or hairline. Head coverings are allowed only if worn for religious or medical reasons.

9. Glasses

Prescription glasses are allowed on United Arab Emirates visa photos. The applicant's eyes must remain fully visible: no flash reflection or glare can be present. Tinted glasses, including sunglasses and prescription lenses, aren't acceptable. If an applicant is wearing glasses for medical reasons, for example, after surgery, a statement from the doctor must be included with the application.

10. UAE Visa Digital Photo Requirements

The image should be high resolution, in focus, sharp, and compression-free. Resolution: at least 600 DPI (1016×1300 pixels), file size between 1 MB and 15 MB, accepted formats: JPG, JPEG, PNG.

11. Print Quality

Photos must be professionally printed on photographic matte or glossy paper. No frames or decorations are allowed. The image must be sharp, free from pixelation, over- or under-exposure, or any other marks.

Unacceptable UAE Visa Photo Examples

Digital vs Paper Emirates Visa Photo Explained

Digital photos are required for online Emirates/Dubai visa photo submissions. The image must be saved as a JPG, JPEG, or PNG file between 1 MB and 15 MB, and have the dimensions of at least 1016×1300 pixels.

Printed photos are required for in-person UAE visa submissions through Emirati consulates, embassies, or authorised agents. Only photos, professionally printed on high-quality photographic paper, either matte or glossy, are accepted. The photo size is 43x55 mm (1.69×2.17 inches), with the face size 31-44 mm (1.2-1.7 inches).

UAE Dependent Visa Photo Requirements


A dependent is a family member who gets a UAE residence visa through a sponsor — usually a spouse, child, or parent who holds a valid UAE residence visa. To qualify, the sponsor must earn at least AED 4,000 per month (or AED 3,000 with company housing) and prove the relationship with attested marriage or birth certificates.

UAE dependent visa photo requirements are identical to those for all other applicants: 

  • The image must be 43 × 55 mm with a plain white background and no shadows. 

  • The dependent’s face should fill 70-80% of the frame, looking directly at the camera with a neutral expression, eyes open, and mouth closed. 

  • Head coverings are only allowed for daily religious wear that doesn’t obscure the face. 

  • Glasses are permitted only if the eyes remain fully visible without glare; tinted lenses are prohibited. 

  • The photo must be taken within the last six months and printed on high-quality photo paper without any digital retouching.

What are the UAE Visa Photo Requirements for Children and Babies?

UAE visa photos for children must follow specific rules so that the image can be used for biometric identification. A child must be photographed alone, facing the camera, with a neutral background and no distracting objects in view. The picture must be sharp, in color, and evenly lit, free of strong shadows, glare, or reflections on the face or in the background.

Infants and Babies Under 1

Newborns and very young babies are photographed lying down, on a plain, light-colored surface such as a sheet or blanket. The camera should be positioned directly above — the baby’s face is clearly visible and centered in the frame. For this age group, it is generally acceptable that the eyes may not fully open or the mouth can be slightly open, provided the facial features are clear and recognisable.

Toddlers and Young Children (Ages 1 to 5)

For toddlers and preschool-age children, the main requirement for a UAE visa photo is that the face is visible and unobstructed. A perfectly neutral expression can be difficult to achieve at this age, so a natural, relaxed look is usually acceptable as long as the child is facing the camera. No toys, pacifiers, furniture, or adults should appear in the image, and the background must remain plain.

Older Children (Ages 6 to 15)

Older children are expected to follow the same UAE visa photo standards as adults. They should sit or stand upright, look directly into the camera, and maintain a calm, neutral expression with their mouth closed. The eyes must be open and clearly visible, and the entire head and upper shoulders should be within the frame.

Taking photos of your child in the studio can be overwhelming, but today, with online photo-making tools, you can avoid a visit to the professional photographer and obtain a fully compliant image at home. Below are a few essentials to keep in mind.

8 Common Reasons for an UAE Visa Photo Rejection


Below is a list of the most common reasons behind an UAE visa photo rejection. 

  1. Wrong photo size. Even the slightest difference in the UAE visa photo size can cause rejection by authorities. The exact size is 43x55 mm, with the head taking 70-80% of the shot.

  2. Incorrect framing. Your UAE visa photo will be rejected if the head is tilted or not centred in the frame. You must look straight at the camera, with head and shoulders fully visible. 

  3. Non‑white background. A UAE visa photo is refused if the background is not plain white. Any colour tint, pattern, texture, or shadows behind the applicant count as a defect.

  4. Exaggerated facial expressions. If the applicant is smiling, frowning, or showing any other exaggerated expressions, a visa photo won’t be accepted.

  5. Glasses blocking the eyes. A visa photo will not be accepted if the glasses hide the eyes. Glare on lenses, thick frames covering the eyes, tinted lenses, or sunglasses are common reasons for rejection.

  6. Obstructed facial features. The photo will be refused if headwear or accessories obscure facial features. 

  7. Poor image quality. Blurred focus, noise, strong filters, over‑ or under‑exposure, or heavy shadows are typical grounds for refusal.

  8. Wrong digital dimensions. If the image has a resolution lower than 600 DPI (about 1016×1300 pixels), the file size is outside the 1-15 MB range, or the file is provided in a format other than JPG, JPEG, or PNG format, it will not be accepted.

Who Needs a UAE Visa and How to Apply

For a short-term stay, most foreigners either enter the UAE visa‑free with a visa on arrival. If your nationality is not eligible for visa‑free entry, or you plan to stay in the Emirates for an extended period, you must obtain a visit or tourist visa before travelling. 

You can apply for a UAE visit visa through several official channels:

  • UAE government e‑portal ICP Smart Services 

  • Registered travel agencies and tour operators that submit applications via approved UAE partners

  • UAE missions abroad — embassies and consulates 

Required Documents for a Dubai Visit Visa

According to the ICP official website, the following documents are required for obtaining a UAE visa:

  • Passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry

  • Technically compliant biometric passport-size photo

  • Valid health insurance policy with coverage within the UAE

  • Confirmed return or onward travel ticket

  • If a UAE resident is sponsoring the trip: the minimum monthly salary is AED 4,000 for first‑degree relatives, AED 8,000 for second‑ and third‑degree relatives, and AED 15,000 for friends, plus proof of kinship for sponsored family members according to the degree of relationship

  1. Recency: Taken within the last 6 months.

  3. Color: Color photo; natural skin/hair tones.

  4. Background: Plain white; no shadows, patterns, or objects.

  5. Lighting: Even lighting; no shadows or glare.

  6. Positioning & framing: Straight to camera; head and shoulders square in the shot; no borders/margins.

  7. Facial expression: Neutral; eyes open; mouth closed.

  8. Attire/head covering/accessories: Normal clothing; no military or camouflage; only religious/medical head coverings are allowed if they don’t obstruct the face and hairline.

  9. Glasses: Allowed if eyes are visible, lenses are free from glare; tinted lenses and sunglasses aren’t acceptable.

  10. Digital requirements: Sharp, high-resolution of 600 DPI (1016×1300 px); 1-15 MB; JPG/JPEG/PNG.

  11. Print quality: High-quality print on photo paper; no visible pixels, blur, banding, stains, or compression artifacts.

What are the Background Color and Lighting Requirements for UAE Visa Photos?

The background must be light-colored, white, or off-white; plain, free from patterns, textures, or shadows.

What Are the UAE Golden Visa Photo Requirements?

UAE golden visa photo requirements follow the same rules set by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs, and Port Security (ICP) for all other visa categories:

  • The photograph must measure 43 × 55 mm with a plain white background covering the entire frame. 

  • The face must occupy 70-80% of the image (31-44 mm from chin to crown), centered and looking directly at the camera with a neutral expression—mouth closed, eyes open, no smiling. 

  • The image must be taken within the last six months, printed in high resolution on photo-quality paper without pixelation or compression artifacts. 

  • Head coverings are permitted only for daily religious attire that does not shadow the face.

  • Tinted glasses and sunglasses are prohibited, while prescription glasses are allowed only if the eyes remain fully visible without glare on the lens.

requirements/uk-passport-photo-requireme.content:
A correctly taken UK passport photo is an essential part of a successful application. It must follow a strict set of rules set by the British government, including proper 35×45 mm sizing and a plain, light‑coloured background, or a 600×750-pixel image in a 50 KB–10 MB JPEG file for digital submissions. This 2026 passport photo requirements, UK Guide includes all the recent official information on passport photo standards — by following them, you will create a compliant photo with a high chance of acceptance. PhotoGov converts a selfie into a file that follows those specifications, ready for His Majesty's Passport Office.

12 Essential Passport Photo Requirements in the UK: Checklist

Source: HM Passport Office

The British passport photo requirements are determined by His Majesty's Passport Office and are based on the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303 biometric standards. When using the PhotoGov online passport photo generator, adherence to the official guidelines is automatic: the UK passport photo you create meets the correct size, crop, proportions, and background requirements. Below is a full list of 12 guidelines for a United Kingdom passport photo. Visa applicants go through a different authority, and our UK visa photo maker prepares the file they need.

Requirement

Details

1. Number of Photos

Two printed photos are required for in-person submissions. One digital photo is required when applying for a British passport online.

2. Recency

Your photo must be taken within the last month, even if your appearance hasn't changed.

3. Countersigning

A new passport photo must be signed by a British citizen in case you are applying for a first adult or child passport, replacing a lost, stolen, or damaged passport, renewing a passport for a child aged 11 or younger, or renewing because your appearance has changed and you are no longer recognisable in your current passport. Read the section below this checklist for more information.

4. UK Passport Photo Size

35 × 45 mm, with a full head measuring 29-34 mm from the crown to the chin for in-person submissions. 600 × 750 pixels for online submissions.

5. Colour

Only coloured photos are accepted with British passport applications, with the colour unaltered by computer software.

6. Background

Plain light-coloured background — plain cream or light grey.

7. Lighting

A photo must be sharp, properly lit, and free of reflections or shadows on your face. The applicant's figure must be in clear contrast to the background. Skin tones must appear natural.

8. Positioning and Framing

An applicant must look straight at the camera with the face, shoulders, and upper body square in the shot. A head close-up takes about 75% of the shot.

9. Facial Expression

A neutral facial expression is required. The applicant's eyes must be open, and their mouth closed. Smiling or any exaggerated emotions may cause the application to be delayed or rejected.

10. Attire, Head Coverings, and Accessories

Regular street clothes in solid, contrasting colours that stand out against the cream background are required. Head coverings must not appear in the image unless they are worn for religious or medical reasons, and in all cases must leave the full face visible. If a head covering is required for medical reasons, the applicant must provide a signed doctor's statement confirming the medical condition. Anything covering your face (accessories, jewellery, scarves) isn't allowed on UK passport pictures.

11. Glasses

No glasses — is the HM Passport Office recommendation. However, if the applicant must wear glasses (for medical reasons), the frames must not cover the eyes, and no glare or flash reflections can be present. Sunglasses or tinted glasses aren't allowed.

12. Print and Digital Quality

A British passport photo must be professionally printed on plain white photographic paper (matte or glossy) without frames or borders. A digital passport photo for online submission must be of high resolution (600 DPI), at a minimum of 600 × 750 pixels, with a file size from 50 KB to 10 MB.
