Digital vs Paper UK Passport Photo Explained

Your application method dictates the photo format. Online applications require a digital photo (uploaded directly or via a photo code from a booth). Paper applications require two identical printed photos (35 × 45 mm) submitted by post. For a visa application, our UK visa photo guide covers the separate document and its photo requirements.

Both formats share identical content rules: plain light background, neutral expression, no glasses, taken within the last month. However, technical specifications differ. Digital photos must be 600 × 750 pixels minimum, JPEG, 50 KB–10 MB. Printed photos must be on photo-quality paper with gloss or matte finish.

You cannot mix formats: online applicants must use digital photos exclusively; paper applicants cannot upload files. Choose your application channel first — this determines your photo requirements.

When Must a UK Passport Photo be Countersigned?

New UK passport photos must be countersigned for identity verification reasons in the following cases:

  • First adult passport applications
  • First child passport applications
  • Replacement applications for lost, stolen, or damaged passports
  • Renewal applications for passports of children aged 11 or under
  • Renewal applications when the holder’s appearance has changed so much that they can no longer be reliably recognised from the existing passport photo.

Who Can Countersign?

According to HM Passport Office guidelines, the countersignatory must be a British citizen who has known the applicant (or the adult signing the form for a child under 16) for at least two years and can personally identify them. This person must be of good standing in their community or work in (or be retired from) a recognised profession, such as a teacher, accountant, lawyer, nurse, civil servant, or post office official.

The countersignatory cannot:

  • Be related to the applicant by birth or marriage
  • Live at the same address
  • Be in a relationship with the applicant
  • Work for His Majesty's Passport Office.

If the applicant is submitting the documents from outside the UK, the countersignatory must hold a current British, Irish, EU, US, or Commonwealth passport.

Can a Friend Sign a Passport Photo?

Yes, a friend can sign a UK passport photo, but only if they meet the official countersignatory criteria.

  • They must have known the applicant personally for at least 2 years (as a friend, neighbour, or colleague), be at least 18, and be able to confirm the applicant’s identity.
  • They must be a person of good standing in the community or work in (or be retired from) a recognised profession (for example, teacher, accountant, lawyer, civil servant, nurse).
  • They cannot be related by birth or marriage, live at the same address, be in a relationship with the applicant, or be involved in the application in an official capacity.

If all these conditions are met, a friend is permitted to sign (or countersign) the passport photo and application.

How Should the UK Passport Photo Be Countersigned?

For paper form applications, one new photo must be certified on the back. The countersignatory should write a brief declaration: “I certify that this is a true likeness of [full name of applicant]”, then add their signature and the date in ink.

The applicant must not write anything on the photos; only the countersignatory verifies their identity as part of the official requirements of His Majesty’s Passport Office.​

Baby Passport Photo Requirements in the UK

Baby passport photo requirements in the UK follow the same core standards as adult applications, but His Majesty's Passport Office allows certain age-based exceptions. The specific requirements depend on your child's age group, as detailed below.

Newborns and Babies Under 1

Newborns may be photographed lying on a plain light‑coloured sheet, with the picture taken from above to avoid shadows on the face or background. The image must be a clear, recent colour photo that meets the standard UK passport requirements for lighting, focus, background, and quality.

Babies under 1 do not have to have their eyes wide open, and their mouth may be open. The baby must be safely positioned, with no hands or other people visible in the photo.

Children Aged 1 to 5

For children under 6, a neutral expression and looking directly at the camera are not strictly required, but the face must be clearly visible. Children must be alone in the picture, with no toys, dummies, other people, or visible support in the frame.

Children Aged 6 to 15

Photographs for children aged 6 and over must meet the same standards as adult passport photos. They must look directly at the camera, have a neutral expression with their mouth closed, eyes open and clearly visible, and no one else or any objects may appear in the photo.

Passport Photo Near Me: The Most Convenient UK Locations

Asking yourself, “Where can I get professional photos that fully meet UK passport photo requirements near me or online”? You’ve got a few options: a photo booth next time you’re shopping for groceries, a high-street photo shop near work, a service at the local post office, or an online tool if you’d rather stay home with a cup of tea.

Photo Booths and Supermarkets

Self-service photo booths are widely available in supermarkets Tesco, Asda, and Sainsbury’s, as well as shopping centres and train stations. These booths provide instant prints and usually a code for online applications. The average price is £5–8, and the service is fast — usually just a few minutes.

Large chains such as Timpson and Max Spielmann, Snappy Snaps, and select pharmacies offer walk-in passport photo services. Staff help ensure the photo meets HMPO requirements and print quality is professional. Prices typically range from £10–15, and you get both digital and print formats.

Post Office ‘Check & Send’ Service

Many Post Office branches offer a ‘Check & Send’ service where staff take your photo, check it meets official requirements, and upload or attach it to your application. The process is reliable, though costs are around £16, and not every location provides this service.

Professional Photographers and Studios

If you want personalised service or need a photo for a baby or someone with special needs, photography studios create high-quality, compliant images. Expect to pay £15 or more, and allow time for travel and possible appointment scheduling.

Online Tools

Online passport photo makers like PhotoGov allow you to instantly create ID photos from the comfort of your home or office. All you need to do is take a selfie with your iPhone or digital camera, upload it to the service, wait about 30 seconds, and download a digital file or a PDF sheet with four printable images. Your passport photos are double-checked for HMPO compliance, and you avoid the need to travel or queue. How to Take a British Passport Photo at Home?

For your picture to match official photo requirements for the UK passport, you must create a simple setup and follow a few basic tips:

  • Find a spot with good lighting and a plain background. Use a tripod or ask someone to take the photo for you. Stand 5-7 feet (1.5-2.1 m) away from the camera.
  • Stand straight, shoulders square to the camera, and look straight into the lens. If taking a selfie, hold the phone steadily at roughly 20 inches (50 cm) from your face.
  • Keep a neutral expression. Keep your eyes open and mouth closed. Make sure that nothing obstructs your facial features. Avoid any head coverings unless they are worn for religious or medical reasons.
  • Take a few shots, and choose the best one. Use the PhotoGov platform to upload and process your photo to the HM Passport Office requirements.
  • Choose additional services such as clothing adjustment or human verification.
  • Download the final image in a digital or printable format.

Common Reasons for a UK Passport Photo Rejection

If you’re asking yourself, “What are the main UK passport photo requirements that cause applications to be rejected and how can I avoid these issues?”, use this checklist with the 12 most common British passport photo rejection reasons:

  1. Incorrect dimensions: The submitted photo does not meet the required size; printed images are not exactly 45 × 35 mm, or digital photos are below 600 × 750 pixels.
  2. Improper background: The background is not plain cream or light grey; instead, it appears white, off-white, patterned, textured, or coloured.
  3. Shadows on the face or background: visible shadows are present on the face or background as a result of uneven or insufficient lighting.
  4. Non-neutral expression: The applicant is not maintaining a neutral facial expression (mouth not fully closed, smiling, frowning, raised eyebrows, or other exaggerated expressions).
  5. Obstructed facial features: Key biometric areas (eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth, or facial contour) are partially covered or obscured by hair, shadows, accessories, or head coverings.
  6. Glasses in the photo: HMPO only allows glasses that are necessary for medical reasons (for example, after an eye surgery). All other glasses must be removed.
  7. Head coverings: Non‑religious or non‑medical headwear is worn, or permitted coverings obscure the face or cast shadows on facial features.
  8. Poor technical quality: The image is blurry, pixelated, out of focus, improperly exposed, or the file size is outside the accepted 50 KB–10 MB range.
  9. Outdated photographs: The photo was taken more than one month before submission.​
  10. Cropped or digitally altered images: The image has been modified with filters, retouching, beauty modes, heavy post-processing, or manual cropping that affects the original composition.
  11. Inappropriate clothing: The applicant is wearing a uniform, camouflage, or clothing that blends into the background or resembles official attire.
  12. Foreign objects or people in infant photos: Objects or other persons are visible in the frame, such as toys, pacifiers, furniture, or supporting hands.

What to Do if Your UK Passport Photo is Rejected

If His Majesty's Passport Office rejects your photo, you must submit a new compliant image. For online applications, simply upload a replacement digital photo through the government portal. For paper applications, include new printed photos with your paperwork. You can use the official online photo checker to verify compliance before submission. If your application is already in progress, HMPO will contact you requesting a replacement, which may extend your passport processing timeline.

What are the Current UK Passport Photo Requirements for Adults and Children to Ensure My Application is Accepted the First Time?

Below is a list of current UK passport photo requirements for adults and children. Follow them to ensure your UK passport application is accepted the first time.

Photo format:

  • Online: 1 digital photo (600 × 750 pixels min, JPEG, 50 KB–10 MB)
  • Paper: 2 identical printed photos (45 × 35 mm, photo-quality paper)
  • Taken within the last month, even if your appearance hasn't changed

Photo content:

  • Full head and shoulders, facing forward, looking at the camera
  • Plain cream or light grey background, no shadows
  • Neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open, face fully visible
  • No glasses recommended; no head coverings (except religious/medical)
  • No other people, toys, or dummies in the frame

Children under 6:

  • Under 1: May lie on a plain sheet, eyes and mouth may be closed/open, no visible hands or support
  • Ages 1–5: Do not need to look directly at the camera or maintain a neutral expression, as long as the face is fully visible.

Children 6+:

  • Same standards as adults (neutral expression, eyes open, mouth closed)

What Size and Dimensions are Required for a UK Passport Photo, and How do I Avoid Common Rejection Reasons?

Here are the standard dimensions for a UK passport photo in different units:

  • UK passport photo size in mm. The United Kingdom passport photo size is 35 x 45 mm.
  • UK passport photo size in cm. The British passport size in cm is 3.5 x 4.5 cm.
  • UK passport photo size in inches. The UK passport photo size in inches is 1.38 x 1.77.
  • UK passport photo size in pixels. The minimum digital size is 600 x 750 pixels. However, many services support higher resolutions. For example, the digital photo size width can be 826 pixels, with a length of 1062 pixels at 600 DPI.

To avoid common rejection reasons for your UK passport photo:

  • Take the photo within the last month, even if your appearance has not changed
  • Use a plain cream or light grey background with no shadows, patterns, or objects visible
  • For printed photos: size 35x45 mm, printed on photo-quality paper, do not crop or cut yourself, no creases or marks
  • For digital photos: 600 x 750 pixels, JPEG format, file is between 50 KB and 10 MB with no compression artifacts
  • Maintain a neutral expression: mouth closed, eyes open and clearly visible, no smiling or frowning
  • Remove glasses to avoid glare and ensure your eyes are fully visible
  • Keep hair away from your face; no hair covering eyes
  • Submit a true, unedited likeness with no filters, digital alterations, red-eye correction, or retouching

How Many Photos are Needed for a UK Passport Application?

Two printed photos are needed for paper form submissions. One digital photo is required for online submissions.

What Are The Official UK Passport Photo Rules For Background, Lighting, and Face Position When Taking Photos At Home?

Here are six tips to take a good-quality picture at home:

  1. Set up a plain, light-coloured background (cream or light grey) with even lighting and no visible shadows.
  2. Stand or sit facing the camera directly, keep your head straight, look into the lens, and maintain a neutral expression with your mouth closed and eyes clearly visible.
  3. Frame a close-up of your full head and upper shoulders so that the head occupies the correct portion of the image without cutting off hair or chin.

Can You Wear Glasses in Passport Photo UK?

Yes, you can — if you genuinely need them for medical reasons. However, the HM Passport Office strongly advises against it as frames can obstruct your eyes and facial features, and lenses often have glare or reflection from the flash. If you can avoid wearing glasses, do so to reduce the risk of your application being delayed or rejected.

What Happens if Passport Photo Rejected UK?

If a UK passport photo is rejected, the application is not immediately refused, but it will be delayed until a new photo is provided.

Here is what typically happens:

  • HM Passport Office pauses processing and sends a notification (by email or post) explaining that the photo does not meet the rules and giving a deadline to submit a replacement.​
  • If you provide a new digital photo for online submission or send new, compliant, printed photos for paper submission within the specified timeframe, the application resumes and continues through the normal processing stages.​
  • If you miss the deadline or never send an acceptable photo, the application can be cancelled, and you may need to apply again and pay the fee a second time.​

So the main risks are extra waiting time and, if you do not fix the problem in time, losing the fee and having to restart the application.

Can You Smile in a Passport Photo UK?

No. You cannot smile, frown, or show any exaggerated emotions in passport pictures, according to the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) biometric standards.

What Are the UK Passport Photo Requirements for Digital Applications, and How Can I Upload a Compliant Image Online?

Below are the UK passport photo requirements for digital uploads, as well as recommendations on the upload process.

Digital photo requirements:

What Clothing And Appearance Rules Do I Need To Follow To Meet UK Passport Photo Requirements And Get Fast Approval?

Clothing requirements

  • Avoid white or very light colours that may blend with the cream or light grey background

mainEntity.name: What are the current UK passport photo requirements for adults and children to ensure my application is accepted the first time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Below is a list of current UK passport photo requirements for adults and children. Photo format: Online applications require 1 digital photo (minimum 600 × 750 pixels, JPEG, 50 KB–10 MB). Paper applications require 2 identical printed photos (45 × 35 mm, photo-quality paper). Photos must be taken within the last month, even if your appearance has not changed. Photo content: The image must show the full head and shoulders, facing forward and looking at the camera, against a plain cream or light grey background with no shadows. The expression must be neutral, with mouth closed, eyes open, and face fully visible. Glasses are not recommended and head coverings are not allowed unless worn for religious or medical reasons. No other people, toys, or dummies may appear in the frame. Children under 6: Babies under 1 year may lie on a plain sheet, with eyes and mouth open or closed, and no visible hands or support. Children aged 1–5 do not need to look directly at the camera or maintain a neutral expression, as long as the face is fully visible. Children aged 6 and above must follow the same standards as adults: neutral expression, eyes open, and mouth closed.

mainEntity.name: What size and dimensions are required for a UK passport photo, and how do I avoid common rejection reasons?

acceptedAnswer.text: The standard UK passport photo size in millimetres is 35 × 45 mm. In centimetres, this is 3.5 × 4.5 cm, and in inches it is 1.38 × 1.77 inches. The minimum digital size is 600 × 750 pixels, although many services support higher resolutions; for example, digital photos can be 826 × 1062 pixels at 600 DPI. To avoid common rejection reasons, take the photo within the last month, use a plain cream or light grey background with no shadows, patterns, or objects visible, and ensure printed photos are 35 × 45 mm on photo-quality paper with no creases or marks. For digital photos, use a 600 × 750 pixel JPEG file between 50 KB and 10 MB, without compression artefacts. Maintain a neutral expression, with mouth closed and eyes open and clearly visible, and avoid smiling or frowning. Remove glasses to reduce glare and ensure your eyes are fully visible. Keep hair away from your face so it does not cover your eyes, and submit a true, unedited likeness with no filters, digital alterations, red-eye correction, or retouching.

mainEntity.name: How many photos are needed for a UK passport application?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two printed photos are needed for paper form submissions. One digital photo is required for online submissions.

mainEntity.name: What are the official UK passport photo rules for background, lighting, and face position when taking photos at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: To take a good-quality UK passport photo at home, set up a plain, light-coloured background (cream or light grey) with even lighting and no visible shadows. Stand or sit facing the camera directly, keep your head straight, look into the lens, and maintain a neutral expression with your mouth closed and eyes clearly visible. Frame a close-up of your full head and upper shoulders so that the head occupies the correct portion of the image without cutting off the hair or chin. Turn off portrait mode so the photo is in sharp focus and in colour. Remove glasses, sunglasses, tinted lenses, or head coverings unless required for religious or medical reasons. Take several shots and upload the best selfie to PhotoGov, which adjusts your image to meet HM Passport Office and ICAO requirements. The final photo is unaltered by computer software, only cropped, resized, and aligned to the required format so that facial features remain completely authentic.

mainEntity.name: Where can I get a passport photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can get your passport photo taken at convenient locations such as photo booths, supermarkets, post offices, and professional studios. If you want to save time and money, you can use an online passport photo maker like PhotoGov, available 24/7 from any location with just a smartphone or laptop. Take a selfie, upload it to the system, and receive a 100% HM Passport Office-compliant passport photo in under 30 seconds. PhotoGov also offers add-on services such as clothing adjustment or human verification for applicants who prefer an additional level of assurance.

mainEntity.name: Can you wear glasses in a UK passport photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can wear glasses in a UK passport photo if you genuinely need them for medical reasons, but the HM Passport Office strongly advises against it. Frames can obstruct your eyes and facial features, and lenses often produce glare or reflections from the flash. If you can avoid wearing glasses, it is better to do so to reduce the risk of your application being delayed or rejected.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a UK passport photo is rejected?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a UK passport photo is rejected, the application is not immediately refused but will be delayed until a new photo is provided. HM Passport Office pauses processing and sends a notification by email or post explaining that the photo does not meet the rules and giving a deadline to submit a replacement. If you upload a new digital photo for an online application or send new compliant printed photos for a paper submission within the specified timeframe, the application resumes and continues through normal processing. If you miss the deadline or never send an acceptable photo, the application can be cancelled and you may need to apply again and pay the fee a second time. The main risks are extra waiting time and, if you do not fix the problem in time, losing the fee and having to restart the application.

mainEntity.name: Can you smile in a UK passport photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. You cannot smile, frown, or show any exaggerated emotions in UK passport photos. According to International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) biometric standards, you must maintain a neutral expression with your mouth closed and eyes open.

mainEntity.name: What are the UK passport photo requirements for digital applications, and how can I upload a compliant image online?

acceptedAnswer.text: For digital UK passport applications, your photo must meet the following requirements: a minimum resolution of 600 × 750 pixels, JPEG format only, file size between 50 KB and 10 MB, full colour (not black and white), and taken within the last month. You can upload online in two ways. Using a photo code: obtain a digital code from a photo booth or shop and enter it during your application to link the photo automatically. For direct upload, select “I'll take or upload a digital photo” during your online application, choose your JPEG file, confirm it meets the rules, and continue. Note that online applications require digital photos only; printed photos (45 × 35 mm) are accepted only with paper applications submitted by post.

mainEntity.name: What are the UK passport photo requirements for babies and children, and where can I get kid-compliant photos taken?

acceptedAnswer.text: UK passport photo requirements for children vary slightly by age. Infants under 1 year may lie on a plain light-coloured sheet, with the photo taken from above; their eyes do not need to be open, and their mouth may be open. The head may be supported by a hand, but the hand must not be visible in the photo, and no toys or dummies are allowed. Children aged 1–5 do not need to look directly at the camera and do not need a neutral expression; smiling is allowed, provided the face is clearly visible and there are no toys, dummies, or visible support in the frame. School-age children 6–15 must follow the same standards as adults: neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open, looking directly at the camera, and no head coverings except for religious or medical reasons. All ages must be alone in the picture, against a plain cream or light grey background, with photos taken within the last month and with good contrast and no shadows. You can get compliant photos from photo booths (with digital codes or printed photos), retail stores such as Boots, Tesco, Asda, Timpson, and Max Spielmann, professional photo studios, or by using the PhotoGov passport photo maker at home, which automatically adjusts your selfie to HM Passport Office requirements.

mainEntity.name: What are the UK passport photo specifications for printed photos and where can I order high-quality compliant prints online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Printed UK passport photos must meet these HM Passport Office specifications: 2 identical photos, each 45 × 35 mm, with face size between 29 and 34 mm from crown to chin. They must be printed professionally, sharp, and in focus on plain white photographic paper with no borders, in perfect condition without creases or marks, and unaltered by software. You can order compliant prints online from services such as Zippi, which offers 8 UK-regulation prints (35 × 45 mm) with trim marks and next-day delivery; Pixum, which provides 8 passport photos (35 × 45 mm) for a fixed price using an online editor; Photo-Me, which delivers professional booth-quality prints with an optional digital photo code; and Passport Photo Digital, which supplies a verified UK passport photo code and optional printed photos checked against HM Passport Office standards. When ordering online, ensure your uploaded image meets all official requirements (600 × 750 pixels, JPEG, 50 KB–10 MB, plain cream or light grey background, neutral expression, no shadows), as services will print exactly what you upload.

mainEntity.name: What clothing and appearance rules do I need to follow to meet UK passport photo requirements and get fast approval?

acceptedAnswer.text: To meet UK passport photo clothing and appearance rules, wear everyday clothing and avoid uniforms or camouflage attire. Do not wear white or very light colours that may blend with the cream or light grey background. Head coverings are not allowed unless worn for religious or medical reasons; if worn, your face must be fully visible from chin to forehead and from edge to edge. Hair must not cover your eyes, so keep it away from your face. Glasses are not recommended, but if you must wear them, there must be no tint, glare, or reflection and the frames must not cover your eyes; sunglasses and tinted lenses are not permitted. Remove headphones, earpieces, or accessories that obscure your face. Maintain a neutral expression with no smiling, frowning, or raised eyebrows; keep your mouth closed and eyes open and clearly visible. Do not use heavy makeup or digital alterations that change your appearance. Avoid uniforms, heavy jewellery that frames the face, hats, caps, and non-religious hair accessories, and anything that casts a shadow on your face. PhotoGov's clothing replacement add-on can upgrade casual clothing to natural-looking formal attire that meets HM Passport Office standards.

mainEntity.name: How can I check if my selfie meets UK passport photo requirements before I pay for my passport application?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can check your selfie for free using PhotoGov's UK passport photo checker before submitting your application. Upload a selfie taken with your smartphone to PhotoGov. The tool automatically adjusts your photo for size (35 × 45 mm), crops it correctly, removes or optimises the background, and checks lighting. The system verifies that your photo meets HM Passport Office requirements, including neutral expression, lack of shadows, and proper contrast. You can then download a compliant digital photo ready for upload to the official UK passport application. PhotoGov checks that the dimensions are correct (minimum 600 × 750 pixels for digital and 35 × 45 mm for print), that the background is plain cream or light grey, that head positioning and sizing are correct, that expression rules are followed, and that there are no shadows or glare. Using PhotoGov before paying for your passport application helps prevent delays or rejections.

mainEntity.name: How do UK passport photo requirements differ for standard passports versus Emergency Travel Documents when getting photos taken?

acceptedAnswer.text: Photo requirements for Emergency Travel Documents (ETDs) are identical to those for standard UK passports: photos must be 45 × 35 mm, taken against a plain cream or light grey background, with a neutral expression, eyes open, and no shadows. However, for ETDs you must apply in person at a consulate or embassy, where photos are checked on the spot. If your photo is rejected, you must provide new ones immediately to avoid delays to urgent travel. Professional verification in advance is strongly recommended before your appointment.

requirements/uk-visa-photo.content:
A UK visa photo is a digital photograph submitted as part of your visa or immigration permission application to the UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI). Unlike many countries that still accept printed passport-style photos at consulates, UKVI now requires all applicants to upload a digital photo through the online application portal or the UK Visas and Immigration: ID Check app.  Our UK passport photo checker turns the same shot into a file for His Majesty's Passport Office.

This Guide covers 2026 UK digital visa photo requirements — from 600 x 750-pixel dimensions and 50 KB-6 MB size to a light-coloured background and “preferably no glasses” rule. Follow them all to avoid a delay or rejection of your Great Britain visa application.

Quick-Reference: UK Visa Photo Specs (UKVI, 2026)


Photo type: Digital upload only 

Minimum size: 600 × 750 pixels

File size: 50 KB – 6 MB

File format: JPG / JPEG only

Background: Plain, light-coloured 

Expression: Neutral, mouth closed, eyes open

Glasses: Not recommended; conditional exception only

Head covering: Only for religious or medical reasons

Photo recency: Taken recently — must reflect current appearance

14 Essential UK Visa Photo Requirements: a Checklist

The UK Visa photo requirements are defined by the UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI), which follow the international biometric standards of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303. All specifications listed in this article reflect the official GOV.UK guidelines as of February 12, 2026.
Your UK digital visa photo must meet them exactly: the image is used for biometric verification during the application, and is matched against your travel document at the point of entry.

Specification

Official Requirement

1. Photo Type

Digital upload only. 

Unlike many countries that still accept printed photos at consulates, UKVI requires all applicants to upload a digital photo through the online application portal or the UK Visas and Immigration: ID Check app. No printed photographs are submitted for standard visa applications.

2. Recency

The photo must have been taken within the last month and accurately reflect your current appearance. 

A significant change — new facial hair, post-surgery changes, or substantial weight change — requires a new photo. 

3. Photo Dimensions

600 x 750 pixels. 

The image must be vertically oriented. Landscape orientation is automatically rejected. There is no specified maximum pixel dimension; the file size limit applies instead.

4. File Size

Minimum 50 KB, maximum 6 MB. 

5. File Format

JPG ( JPEG) only. 

PNG, HEIF, BMP, PDF, and all other formats are not accepted by the UKVI visa portal. 

6. Colour

Only full-colour photographs are accepted. 

Black-and-white, sepia, and colour-filtered images are not permitted. The image must reproduce natural skin tones and facial detail accurately.

7. Background

Plain, light-coloured background only — cream, ivory, off-white, or light grey. 

No textures, patterns, shadows, or objects should be visible. Your face must be in clear contrast to the background. 

8. Lighting

Even, diffuse illumination with no harsh shadows under the nose, chin, or around the ears. 

No flash glare on the forehead. No shadows cast behind you on the background. Natural window light or soft lighting on both sides of the face produces the best results.

9. Positioning and Framing

The applicant must face the camera directly, with the head centred horizontally and vertically in the frame. 

No tilting, turning, or angling of the head. The full head, shoulders, and upper body must be visible and squared to the camera.

10. Facial Expression

A neutral expression is mandatory — both eyes open and fully visible, mouth closed, no smiling, frowning, or squinting. 

No hair covering the eyes or obscuring facial features. Biometric facial recognition systems require relaxed facial muscles for accurate measurement.

11. Attire, Head Coverings, and Accessories

Everyday clothing in solid or plain colours is acceptable. 

Head coverings are permitted only for documented religious or medical reasons — the full face from chin to forehead must remain completely visible. Fashion hats, caps, and decorative headbands are not allowed. All earphones, earbuds, and wireless headsets must be removed.

12. Glasses

Glasses are not recommended. GOV.UK guidance states: “Do not wear glasses in your photo unless you have to.” 

If worn for medical reasons, lenses must be clear — no tinted or darkened lenses — and there must be no glare, reflections, or shadows over the eyes. Glasses frequently cause automated rejection even when the lenses are clear.

13. Editing and Filters

Not permitted. 

The photo must be digitally unaltered — no beauty apps, AI skin-smoothing, Instagram-style filters, background replacement, teeth whitening, or auto-enhance modes. The image must be the original, unedited photograph submitted directly from the camera.

14. Source Device

Photos taken with a phone or tablet are acceptable. 

Professional equipment is not required. Disable all automatic beauty modes, portrait mode, and AI enhancement features before taking the photo. GOV.UK recommends having another person take the photo — selfies are allowed, but produce worse results.

Source: UK Visas and Immigration

⚠️  UKVI Digital-Only Policy (February 2026)

The UK Visas and Immigration guidance page for visa photos was published on 12 February 2026. UKVI now processes applications digitally. Paper photos are no longer submitted at visa application centres for most application types. Always check your specific visa application form for current submission instructions.

How to Submit Your UK Visa Photo in 2026: 3 Official Channels

Since February 2026, the UK visa and immigration permission applications can only be submitted online. Your photo is uploaded directly during the online application process. Choose one of the three submission channels relevant to your case.

1. Online Visa Application Portal

The most common way to apply for a British visa is via the GOV.UK portal. After completing a small questionnaire, you will be guided to a relevant page for your type of application, for example, a Standard visitor visa.

Complete your visa application. You will be prompted to upload your digital photo at the relevant step. The portal automatically checks whether your photo meets the 2026 technical and biometric specifications. If your photo is rejected, you will be prompted to upload another photograph.

2. UK Visas and Immigration: ID Check App

Some applicants can use the UKVI ID Check app to verify their identity and submit their photo from a smartphone. The app includes a built-in photo check that validates lighting, focus, and face positioning in real time. Available for eligible nationalities with biometric passports.

  • Download the ID Check app for Android

  • Download the ID Check app for iPhone

Follow the in-app guidance to complete your visa submission. Please note that Ukrainian citizens are currently unable to use the app for visa applications.

3. Visa Application Centres (VAC)

If you cannot submit biometric information online, you may be required to attend a Visa Application Centre. At the VAC, your biometric data (fingerprints and photograph) is captured digitally by the staff. You do not bring a printed photo to the VAC — the photo is taken there.

How to Take a Compliant UK Visa Photo at Home

Set up the Shot

Start with your background: find a plain, light-coloured wall or hang a plain cream/white/light grey sheet — no texture, no pattern, nothing behind you. Before you do anything else, set up your lighting. Face a window with natural daylight, or use two soft light sources on either side of your face to eliminate shadows. 

Prepare Your Appearance

Remove glasses if you safely can — the UKVI's automated biometric system checks eye geometry as a core verification step. Glasses — even transparent ones — can interfere with this check and result in photo rejection.

GOV.UK guidance states: "Do not wear glasses in your photo unless you have to." If you must wear glasses (for medical reasons), the following conditions apply:

  • No sunglasses.

  • No tinted lenses — glasses must be clear.

  • Eyes must not be covered by frames.

  • No glare, reflections, or shadows from the lenses.

  • Eyes must be clearly visible.

Head coverings are not permitted in UK visa or passport photos unless worn for religious or medical reasons.

  • Religious head coverings (e.g. hijab, turban, kippah) arepermitted — but your face from the bottom of your chin to the top of your forehead must be fully visible.

  • Medical head coverings (e.g. post-surgical cap) arepermitted with appropriate documentation from the medical provider.

  • Fashion hats, caps, or decorative headbands arenot permitted.

Correctly Frame the Shot 

Frame the shot so your full head, upper shoulders, and clothed torso are in the picture. Before uploading, check that the file is JPG or JPEG, vertically oriented, at least 600×750 pixels, and between 50 KB and 6 MB. Turn off any auto-beautify, portrait mode, or AI enhancement on your phone camera. Filters and AI retouching are prohibited and will cause automatic rejection.

Take the Photo

Have someone else take the photo — don't take a selfie if you can avoid it. A phone or tablet on a stand with a timer works too. Look straight at the camera, keep a completely neutral expression, close your mouth, and make sure both eyes are fully open and visible.

GOV.UK recommends asking someone else to take your photo. Self-photos (selfies) are technically allowed if taken with a phone or tablet, but having another person take the photo reduces the risk of bad angles, shadows, and rejection.

Adjust the Photo to the UK Visa Photo Requirements

Use a reliable online UK visa photo tool to correctly frame, resize, and adjust your original photo to the official 2026 UK photo specs. The PhotoGov UK visa photo editor follows all international biometric photo rules, and doesn’t alter your facial features or skin complexion, providing a technically correct digital image, ready for immediate submission.

Apply for Your UK Visa Photo

Upload directly through the UKVI online portal or the UK Visas and Immigration: ID Check app. The system runs automated biometric quality checks on upload and will flag problems immediately.

UK Visa Photos of Children and Infants

Children applying for a UK visa or passport must meet the same general rules as adults, with the following age-specific exceptions:

Age Group

Exception

Under 6 years

Do not have to be looking directly at the camera or have a plain expression

Under 1 year

Eyes do not have to be open

Under 1 year

Can be supported by a parent's hand — but the hand must not be visible in the photo

Under 1 year

May lie on a plain light-coloured sheet; photo taken from above

All children

Must be alone in the picture — no adults visible

Babies

Must not be holding toys or using dummies

Increase Your Chance of UK Visa Approval: Checklist

Common Reasons for UK Visa Photo Rejection

UKVI's portal and ID Check App perform automated technical and biometric photo checks. Photographs that fail these checks are rejected before the application is processed. Common causes of rejection include:

1. Wrong photo dimensions: Images under 600 × 750 pixels do not contain sufficient resolution for biometric face-matching algorithms to process reliably.

2. File too small or too large: Images under 50 KB are typically too heavily compressed. Compression artefacts distort facial geometry data and trigger automated rejection. Files over 6 MB are automatically rejected.

3. Glasses causing glare or shadow over eyes: Even clear prescription glasses can interfere with the eye geometry check. UKVI strongly recommends removing glasses entirely.

4. Background has shadows or patterns: A non-uniform or patterned background reduces facial contrast and causes the face-detection step to fail.

5. Eyes not open or partially obscured by hair: The system requires both eyes to be fully visible. Hair over the eyes, a heavy fringe, or partially closed eyes will cause the biometric check to fail.

6. Photo is digitally altered or filtered: Any post-processing — including smartphone beauty modes, AI skin-smoothing, teeth whitening, or background replacement — disqualifies the photo. The image must be the unaltered original.

7. Landscape (horizontal) orientation: The system expects portrait orientation. Landscape files are automatically rejected without manual review.

8. Reusing a passport photo: GOV.UK explicitly prohibits submitting the same photo that appears in your passport or identity card. A new photo must be taken for your visa application.

9. Strong expression (smile or frown): Smiling, frowning, or raised eyebrows alter facial landmark geometry. A completely neutral expression with the mouth closed is required.

10. HEIF or PNG format: The UK visa portal accepts JPG/JPEG only. Photos submitted in PNG, HEIF (HEIC), and other formats will be automatically rejected.

11. Head covering (non-religious/medical): Head coverings not worn for religious or medical reasons obstruct biometric head geometry measurements and cause rejection.

What to Do if Your UK Visa Photo Has Been Rejected?

What to Do if Your UK Visa Photo Has Been Rejected?

If the UKVI portal or the ID Check App rejects your photo on upload, read the rejection message carefully — the system usually identifies the specific issue, such as wrong file format, image too small, or a detected quality problem. Correct the flagged issue and re-upload immediately; the portal allows you to retry without restarting your entire application. The most common fixes are: switching from PNG to JPEG, disabling beauty or portrait mode on your phone before retaking the photo, and ensuring the background is plain and shadow-free. If your glasses triggered the rejection, retake without them. If your application has already been submitted and returned due to a photo issue, you will receive a notification with a resubmission deadline — act the same day. If you are directed to a Visa Application Centre (VAC), do not bring printed photos: your biometric photograph is captured digitally by staff on site.

UK Visa Photo vs UK Passport Photo: Key Differences

Both types of photos follow the same general appearance rules. The main practical differences are:

Same Photo Across UK Documents?

You cannot reuse your passport photo for a visa application. GOV.UK guidance explicitly states your photo must not be the same photo that is in your passport or identity card.


UK Photo Format vs International Standards

The UK uses a 35 × 45 mm format for printed photos — the same as the ICAO (International Civil Aviation Organization) Document 9303 standard used in most of Europe and internationally. This makes the UK format compatible with EU visa photos (Germany, France, Netherlands, etc.).

UK Format Is ICAO-Compatible

Because the UK uses the ICAO 35×45mm format, a photo taken to UK visa spec may also be usable for Schengen visa applications and most European identity documents — provided background colour and other local rules are satisfied. Always verify with the destination country's official guidance.

UK Visa Photo Requirements: Final Thoughts

The UK visa photo process in 2026 is fully digital as of February; submitting printed photos with visa agencies or dropping your application off at a consulate isn’t available anymore. 

The UK uses the ICAO 35×45 mm format — compatible with most European documents — but is incompatible with the US 2×2 inch square format. The visa and passport photo rules are nearly identical in appearance, but differ in file specs: visa caps at 6 MB and accepts JPG/JPEG only, while the passport portal also accepts PNG and allows up to 10 MB. You cannot reuse a photo already in your passport — this is explicitly prohibited. You can also make a UK passport photo online, since the appearance rules are nearly identical.

The UKVI's portal and the ID Check App run automated biometric checks, so technical compliance matters as much as your appearance in the shot. 

The two most common failure points are AI-enhanced photos (auto-beauty modes on iPhones, Samsung, and Pixel phones silently alter images) and glasses, which interfere with eye geometry verification even when lenses are clear. Avoid that, and follow the recommendations we provided in this guide, and your photo has a high chance of approval.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Are the Current UK Visa Photo Size Requirements?

Your UK visa photo must be a digital file of at least 600 × 750 pixels (width × height) in portrait/vertical orientation. The file must be between 50 KB and 6 MB, saved in JPG or JPEG format only — PNG, HEIF, BMP, and PDF are not accepted.

The photo must be in full colour with a plain, light-coloured background. Lighting must be even and diffuse, with no harsh shadows on the face, no flash glare, and no red eye. The UKVI portal runs automated biometric checks on upload and flags any file that falls outside these parameters immediately.

Can I Take My Own UK Visa Photo With a Smartphone?

Yes. GOV.UK guidance states that photos can be taken with a phone or tablet. However, you are advised to have another person take the photo for you, as this reduces the risk of poor angles and shadow. Make sure the device camera is set to the highest quality and no filters or beauty modes are active.

What Background Colour is Correct for the UK Visa — White or Light Grey?

For UK visa photos, the UK Visas and Immigration official website says “plain light-coloured background” without specifying a single colour. Acceptable shades include cream, ivory, off-white, and light grey. A bright white background is generally acceptable, but avoid stark white that may cause overexposure and affect facial contrast.

Does the UK Visa Photo Need to be Taken Recently?

Yes. Your photo must accurately reflect your current appearance. UK Visas and Immigration does not specify an exact recency for visa photos specifically, but we recommend using the photo taken within the last month. 

What Are the UK Visa Photo Requirements for Glasses, Beard, and Headwear?

Glasses are not recommended. The official UK Visas and Immigration guidance states: "Do not wear glasses in your photo unless you have to." If worn for a documented medical reason, lenses must be clear — no tinted or darkened glass — and there must be no glare, reflections, or shadows over the eyes, which must remain fully visible. Even clear prescription glasses frequently trigger automated rejection due to interference with the eye geometry biometric check.

Beard and facial hair carry no specific restrictions. Any beard, moustache, or stubble is permitted, provided the face from chin to forehead is clearly visible and the neutral expression requirement is met. If significant facial hair changes occur after the photo was taken, a new photo reflecting your current appearance is required.

Headwear is permitted only for religious or medical reasons:

  • Religious coverings (hijab, turban, kippah) are allowed — but the full face from chin to forehead must remain completely unobstructed

  • Medical head coverings (e.g., post-surgical cap) are permitted with appropriate documentation

  • Fashion hats, caps, and decorative headbands are not permitted under any circumstances.

What Clothes Are Allowed for UK Visa Photos?

Everyday clothing in any colour or plain style is acceptable for a UK visa photo. There are no restrictions on formal, casual, or cultural dress — the rules focus entirely on the head and face area remaining unobstructed.

  • Avoid heavy patterns or prints, which can interfere with facial recognition processing

  • Head coverings are permitted for religious or medical reasons only — a hijab, turban, or kippah is allowed, provided the full face from chin to forehead remains completely visible; fashion hats, caps, and decorative headbands are not permitted

Note that all earphones, earbuds, and wireless headsets must also be removed before the photo is taken.

Can I Wear a Hijab or Religious Head Covering in My UK Visa Photo?

Yes. Head coverings worn for religious or medical reasons are permitted. Your full face from chin to forehead must remain visible and unobstructed in the photo.

My Photo Was Rejected by the UKVI Portal — What Do I Do?

Read the rejection reason displayed on screen. Common issues are file format (must be JPG/JPEG), file too small, or photo not meeting appearance rules. Retake the photo, correcting the flagged issue and re-upload. If you continue experiencing problems, consult the GOV.UK guidance page or contact UKVI customer services.

Can I Use a Photo Booth Photo for My UK Visa Application?

Only if it meets the technical spec: JPG/JPEG format, minimum 600×750 pixels, 50 KB–6 MB, no editing. Modern digital photo booths typically output compliant files. Check that the background is plain light-coloured and the booth does not auto-apply enhancement. Traditional printed photos from photo booths cannot be uploaded directly — you would need to scan them, which UK Visas and Immigration explicitly prohibits ('must not be a scan or photo of another photo of you'). Use a digital-native photo source.

Is the UK Visa Photo the Same as the UK Passport Photo?

No. The UK Visas and Immigration guidance explicitly states that your visa photo must not be the same photo that appears in your passport or identity card — a new photo is required.

The appearance rules for both documents are nearly identical, but the technical specs differ in a few key areas. The visa photo file cap is 6 MB and accepts JPG/JPEG only, while the passport online portal also accepts PNG and allows up to 10 MB. Scanning a printed passport booth photo and uploading it is also prohibited — GOV.UK states the image "must not be a scan or photo of another photo of you." The UK passport photo requirements guide on PhotoGov compares the digital and printed specs side by side.

Do I Need a Paper Photo For a UK Visa Application?

No. In 2026, UKVI processes applications digitally, and your biometric photo is submitted through the online portal or ID Check app. Some older or specialist application routes may still involve a Visa Application Centre visit, where staff capture your biometric data (including photo) digitally. Always check the specific instructions for your visa category.

What Are the UK Visa Photo Requirements for Professional Studio Photography?

As of February 2026, UKVI accepts digital photos only — professional studio equipment is not required. UK Visas and Immigration explicitly states that photos taken with a phone or tablet are fully acceptable, provided the file is JPG/JPEG, at least 600 × 750 pixels, and between 50 KB and 6 MB.

The same core principles that guide studio photography apply regardless of the device:

  • Lighting must be even and diffuse — no flash glare or shadows on the face

  • Background must be plain and light-coloured — cream, ivory, off-white, or light grey

  • Framing must show the full head, upper shoulders, and clothed torso; head centred with no tilting

  • No editing — beauty apps, AI skin-smoothing, filters, and auto-enhance modes are prohibited and cause automatic rejection

UK Visas and Immigration recommends having another person take the photo rather than a selfie, as this reduces the risk of poor angles and shadows.

requirements/us-department-of-state-phot.content:
The US Department of State is the key US authority that sets guidelines for ID photos. That includes pictures for all document types — US visas, US passports, citizenship, DV visa lottery applications, and green cards. This Guide explains all official requirements for all key document types in detail. The information provided here is up to date and verified by our expert in March 2026. The passport rules, including the 2 x 2 inch format, are collected in our US passport photo requirements guide.

About the U.S. Department of State

The U.S. Department of State (DOS) is the federal executive department that oversees the United States’ foreign policy and international relations. It functions as the United States’ foreign ministry and is headed by the Secretary of State, the President’s principal adviser on foreign affairs.

For travelers and migrants, the Department of State serves as the primary authority: it establishes the rules and procedures for U.S. visas and passports, oversees the systems that support international travel, and helps ensure that cross‑border movement remains secure and orderly.

Travel.State.Gov: the Only Website You Need

Travel.State.Gov is the US Department of State’s official website for travel and immigration services. It brings together information and online tools on nonimmigrant and immigrant visas, U.S. passports, and country‑specific travel advisories and safety guidance.

Visas and DV Lottery Photo Guidelines

The U.S. Visas section on Travel.State.Gov covers temporary (nonimmigrant) visas for travel, study, and work, as well as immigrant visas that can lead to permanent residence (green cards) and citizenship (passports).

The Department of State runs the annual Diversity Immigrant Visa Program (DV Lottery), publishing official instructions, eligibility rules, and photo specifications that applicants must follow when submitting their electronic entries.

U.S. Passports and Citizenship Photo Guidelines

The U.S. Passports section is focused on documents for U.S. citizens and nationals. It explains how to apply for or renew a passport, and which technical requirements apply to printed and digital passport photos that must be provided with passport applications.

All the Answers You Need: Travel.State.Gov's FAQ Section

The FAQ Section on the Travel.State.Gov comprehensively covers all questions relevant to visa photo applications. For example, if you have undergone a significant change in appearance, such as major facial surgery or removal of a large facial tattoo, you will need to submit a new photo. Study it carefully before submitting your documents.

The U.S. Department of State’s General Visa Photo Rules

AspectRequirement (All Visa Types)
ColorColor photo, not black-and-white ​
Dimensions2 x 2 inches (51 x 51 mm)
Head sizeHead height 1–1 3/8 in (22–35 mm) or 50–69% of image height from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head
RecencyTaken within the last 6 months and reflecting current appearance ​
BackgroundPlain white or off-white background, with no patterns, objects, or strong shadows
PoseFull-face view, looking into the camera directly, with both eyes open
ExpressionNeutral facial expression, eyes open, mouth closed
ClothingEveryday clothing; no uniforms, except religious clothing worn daily ​
Head coveringsA head covering is allowed only when worn daily for religious purposes; the full face and hairline must remain visible. ​Hair should not obscure the face, and the hairline must remain visible in accordance with the US Department of State photo guidelines
DevicesNo headphones, wireless devices, or similar items; hearing devices may remain if worn daily​
Eye glassesNot allowed
Source qualityPhotos must not be scans or copies of documents; snapshots, magazine photos, vending-machine, or low-quality phone photos. Full-length photos are not acceptable. ​
ReferencesApplicants are advised to review the Official Photo Sample for clear examples of acceptable and unacceptable images

Nonimmigrant Visa Photo Requirements

This page of the U.S. Department of State website sets out the photo requirements for nonimmigrant visa applicants, including those completing Form DS‑160 (tourism, study, temporary employment visas) and Form DS‑1648 (A, G, and NATO visas for employees, officials, and their family members). All key photograph specifications are provided there.

New Photos for Nonimmigrant Visas (DS‑160 / DS‑1648)

All pictures for nonimmigrant visas are uploaded online, together with an application form, In rare cases (for example, when the digital upload fails and your confirmation page shows an “X” instead of your photo), you may be instructed to bring a printed 2 x 2 inch photo together with your DS‑160/DS‑1648 confirmation page to the embassy or consulate, in line with that post’s specific instructions. 

Besides the general specifications, applicants using Forms DS‑160 and DS‑1648 must follow the additional rules:

AspectRequirement (Nonimmigrant Visas)
FormApplicants complete an online Form DS‑160 or DS‑1648 ​
Digital uploadA digital photo must be uploaded as part of the online visa application ​
DimensionsSquare image (1:1); minimum 600 x 600 pixels, maximum 1200 x 1200 pixels ​
File formatJPEG (.jpg)​
Color spaceColor image, 24 bits per pixel, sRGB color space ​
File sizeLess than or equal to 240 kB
Scanned photoIf scanning an existing 2 x 2 inch (51 x 51 mm) photo, the resolution must be 300-600 DPI ​
Printed photoAdditionally, embassies or consulates may require one printed 2 x 2-inch photo on photo‑quality paper. But always check for the exact requirement with your authority
Children’s photosWhen submitting a visa photo for a child, especially infants or toddlers, make sure the background is plain, and there are no visible objects in the frame 
ReferencesApplicants are advised to review the Official Photo Sample for clear examples of acceptable and unacceptable images

Immigrant Visa Photo Requirements

Diversity Visa (DV) Lottery — Online Entry (Digital Image)

This section of the US Department of State website is dedicated to immigrant visa photo requirements. All key photograph specifications may be found there. Besides the general specifications in the table above, the Diversity Visa Program entrants must follow the additional rules when submitting their digital photos:

AspectRequirement (DV Online Entry)
FormApplicants submit an online Diversity Visa (DV) entry form as part of the lottery application.
SubmissionDV entrants must upload a digital photo as part of the online entry
File formatJPEG (.jpg).
File sizeEqual to or less than 240 kB
Aspect ratioSquare image (1:1)
Dimensions600 x 600 pixels, 1200 x 1200 pixels maximum
Scanned photoIf scanning an existing photo, the original must be 2 x 2 in (51 x 51 mm) and scanned at 300 dpi (12 pixels/mm)

Green Card Printed Photo — Interview

Besides the general photo specifications mentioned above, the Diversity Visa Program selectees must bring the following printed photos to their in-person interview.

AspectRequirement (Green Card Interview)
Number of photosTwo identical photos must be provided at the immigrant visa interview
Print qualityPhotos must be printed on high-quality photo paper. ​
SizeEach photo must be 2 x 2 inches (51 x 51 mm).

Passport and Citizenship Photo Requirements

This page of the US Department of State website is dedicated to US passport photo requirements. Find the exact specifications for your particular application:

  • New passport application for adults — follow this link on the US Department of State’s website.
  • New passport application for minors (under the age of 16) — follow this link on the US Department of State’s website.
  • Emergency passport applications (life or death situations, urgent travel) — follow this link on the US Department of State’s website.
  • Online passport renewal — follow this link on the US Department of State’s website.

Passport Photos for Paper Applications

AspectRequirement (Paper Passport Applications)
Number of photosSubmit one photo with your paper application ​
ColorColor photo; black-and-white photos are not accepted. ​
RecencyThe photo must be taken within the last 6 months and reflect your current appearance
Size2 x 2 inches (51 x 51 mm)
Head sizeHead height between 1 and 1 3/8 inches (25–35 mm) from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head
BackgroundWhite or off-white background, without shadows, textures, or patterns
PoseFull-face view, directly facing the camera, no head tilt ​
ExpressionNeutral facial expression, eyes open, mouth closed ​
Image qualityHigh resolution; not blurry, grainy, pixelated, damaged, or over/underexposed ​
Print qualityPrinted on matte or glossy high-quality photo paper; no photocopies or digitally-scanned prints ​
Digital editsDo not alter the photo with software, filters, or artificial intelligence ​
EyeglassesNo glasses; rare medical exceptions require a signed doctor’s note
AttireEveryday clothing; no uniforms, clothing resembling a uniform, or camouflage​
Hats/head coveringsMust be removed unless worn daily for religious or medical reasons; the full face must remain visible ​
AccessoriesNo face coverings or masks; no headphones or wireless devices. Jewelry and facial piercings are allowed only if they do not obscure the face ​
LightingEven lighting across the face and background; no strong shadows or glare

Digital Photos for Online U.S. Passport Renewals

AspectRequirement (Digital Passport Photo)
When usedRequired when renewing a U.S. passport online
File formatsJPG, JPEG, or HEIF
Dimensions600 x 600 pixels
File sizeBetween 54 KB and 10 MB
Color & recencyMust be in color and taken within the last 6 months
BackgroundWhite or off-white, plain, free from shadows, patterns, or textures
EditingNo digital alterations are allowed
Upload methodSelect a photo from your device or drag and drop it into the online application.
Manual reviewA passport employee reviews the photo again after submission; if there is a problem, you receive a letter or email asking for a new photo.

The US Department of State, and its official website Travel.State.Gov, is the official resource for all information on visa and passport photos in the United States.
